--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelogs/fragments/password-lookup-and-hash-ident.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+minor_changes:
+  - password lookup - new ``ident`` parameter to select the bcrypt ident (``2``, ``2a``, ``2b`` or ``2y``) when using ``encrypt=bcrypt``; when ``encrypt=bcrypt`` and no ``ident`` is given, ``2a`` is used.  The chosen ident is stored in the password file together with the salt so that repeated runs reproduce the same choice.
+  - password_hash filter - new optional ``ident`` parameter to select the bcrypt ident (``2``, ``2a``, ``2b`` or ``2y``) for ``blowfish``/bcrypt hashes; for other algorithms the parameter is accepted but has no effect.
diff --git a/docs/docsite/rst/user_guide/playbooks_filters.rst b/docs/docsite/rst/user_guide/playbooks_filters.rst
index d7907d101c..ae61914d50 100644
--- a/docs/docsite/rst/user_guide/playbooks_filters.rst
+++ b/docs/docsite/rst/user_guide/playbooks_filters.rst
@@ -1335,6 +1335,15 @@ Some hash types allow providing a rounds parameter::
     {{ 'secretpassword' | password_hash('sha256', 'mysecretsalt', rounds=10000) }}
     # => "$5$rounds=10000$mysecretsalt$Tkm80llAxD4YHll6AgNIztKn0vzAACsuuEfYeGP7tm7"
 
+The ``blowfish`` (aka bcrypt) hash type also allows providing an ``ident`` parameter to select
+the bcrypt variant ("ident") that is written into the resulting hash.  The supported values are
+``2``, ``2a``, ``2b`` and ``2y`` (for example some environments only accept the older ``$2a$``
+ident).  When no ``ident`` is given the default used by the underlying library is kept.  For all
+other hash types the ``ident`` parameter is accepted but has no effect::
+
+    {{ 'secretpassword' | password_hash('blowfish', 'mysecretsalt', ident='2a') }}
+    # => "$2a$12$mysecretsalt...."
+
 .. _other_useful_filters:
 
 Manipulating text

+    from a configurable list of sources.

+    runtime files (such as C(/proc/mounts)) and the output of the C(mount)

+    statistics (C(size_total) and C(size_available)) with C(df) for every

+  devices:
+    description:

+        mounts by device name.
+      - Only mounts whose device matches at least one of the patterns are
+        returned. If omitted, no device filtering is applied.
+    type: list
+    elements: str
+  fstypes:
+    description:

+      - Only mounts whose filesystem type matches at least one of the

+        V(static), V(dynamic) or V(mount).

+        configured through O(mount_binary).
+      - The alias V(all) expands to V(static), V(dynamic) and V(mount).
+    type: list
+    elements: str
+    default:
+      - all
+  mount_binary:
+    description:
+      - Path to the C(mount) executable used to gather mount information when
+        V(mount) (or V(all)) is part of O(sources).
+      - If omitted, the C(mount) executable is looked up in the C(PATH)
+        environment variable.
+    type: str
+  timeout:
+    description:
+      - Maximum time in seconds to wait for gathering the mount information,
+        including reading the sources and fetching the per mount details
+        (UUID resolution and disk usage statistics).
+      - What happens when the timeout is exceeded is controlled by
+        O(on_timeout).
+    type: float
+    default: 10
+  on_timeout:
+    description:
+      - Action to take when O(timeout) is exceeded.
+      - With V(error) the module fails, partially gathered facts are still
+        returned.
+      - With V(warn) a warning is issued and the mounts that could not be
+        enriched are returned without size information.
+      - With V(ignore) the timeout is silently ignored and the affected
+        mounts are returned without size information.
+    type: str
+    choices:
+      - error
+      - warn
+      - ignore
+    default: warn
+  include_aggregate_mounts:
+    description:
+      - When true, the complete list of all discovered mounts, including
+        duplicate mount points reported by several sources, is returned in
+        C(aggregate_mounts).
+      - When a mount point is reported by more than one source and this
+        option is not true, a warning is issued about the duplicate mount
+        points.
+    type: bool
+    default: false
+requirements:
+  - The C(df) utility (coreutils) is only required to collect the disk usage
+    statistics (C(size_total) and C(size_available)). If it is not available
+    or fails, the size related facts are left empty.
+notes:
+  - This module is meant for POSIX systems, on other platforms the sources
+    may not exist and no facts will be gathered.
+  - Mount points reported by more than one source are only returned once in
+    C(mount_points), the first occurrence in source order wins.
+  - The C(source) fact of each mount entry describes where the mount was
+    gathered from, either a source file path or V(mount) for the output of
+    the mount binary.
+author:
+  - Ansible Core Team
+extends_documentation_fragment:
+  - action_common_attributes
+  - action_common_attributes.facts
+attributes:
+  check_mode:
+    support: full
+  diff_mode:
+    support: none
+  facts:
+    support: full
+  platform:
+    platforms: posix
+"""
+
+EXAMPLES = r"""
+# Gather mount facts from all default sources (/etc/fstab, /proc/mounts and the mount binary)
+- ansible.builtin.mount_facts:
+
+# Gather the mounted filesystems only, restricted to GPFS and FUSE filesystems
+- ansible.builtin.mount_facts:
+    sources:
+      - dynamic
+    fstypes:
+      - gpfs
+      - fuse*
+
+# Gather all mounts with a device matching /dev/sd* and keep the complete
+# list of duplicates
+- ansible.builtin.mount_facts:
+    devices:
+      - /dev/sd*
+    include_aggregate_mounts: true
+
+# Use a custom mount binary and fail after 5 seconds if the gathering times out
+- ansible.builtin.mount_facts:
+    sources:
+      - /etc/fstab
+      - mount
+    mount_binary: /bin/mount
+    timeout: 5
+    on_timeout: error
+"""
+
+RETURN = r"""
+ansible_facts:
+  description:
+    - Facts about the gathered filesystem mounts.
+    - Mount points reported by more than one source are only listed once in
+      C(mount_points), use O(include_aggregate_mounts) to also get the
+      complete list of all discovered mounts in C(aggregate_mounts).
+  returned: always
+  type: complex
+  contains:
+    mount_points:
+      description:
+        - Dictionary of the unique mount points that were discovered.
+        - The keys are the mount points, each value is an object describing
+          the mount.
+      returned: always
+      type: dict
+      sample:
+        "/":
+          device: /dev/sda1
+          mount: /
+          fstype: ext4
+          options: rw,relatime
+          dump: 1
+          passno: 1
+          uuid: 12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc
+          size_total: 1024000000
+          size_available: 512000000
+          source: /proc/mounts
+    aggregate_mounts:
+      description:
+        - List of all discovered mounts, including mount points that are
+          reported by more than one source.
+      returned: when O(include_aggregate_mounts) is true
+      type: list
+      elements: dict
+      contains:
+        device:
+          description:
+            - Device the filesystem is mounted from. UUID form devices
+              (such as C(UUID=...)) are resolved to the device path when
+              possible.
+          returned: always
+          type: str
+        mount:
+          description: Mount point of the filesystem.
+          returned: always
+          type: str
+        fstype:
+          description: Filesystem type.
+          returned: always
+          type: str
+        options:
+          description: Mount options as reported by the source.
+          returned: always
+          type: str
+        dump:
+          description:
+            - Dump frequency of the filesystem as reported by the source,
+              null when the source does not provide it.
+          returned: always
+          type: int
+        passno:
+          description:
+            - Pass number for fsck as reported by the source, null when the
+              source does not provide it.
+          returned: always
+          type: int
+        uuid:
+          description:
+            - UUID of the device when it could be determined, otherwise
+              C(N/A).
+          returned: always
+          type: str
+        size_total:
+          description:
+            - Total size of the filesystem in bytes, as reported by C(df).
+            - Null when the size could not be determined, for example
+              because the mount point does not exist, C(df) is not
+              available or a timeout occurred.
+          returned: always
+          type: int
+        size_available:
+          description:
+            - Available size of the filesystem in bytes, as reported by
+              C(df).
+            - Null when the size could not be determined, for example
+              because the mount point does not exist, C(df) is not
+              available or a timeout occurred.
+          returned: always
+          type: int
+        source:
+          description:
+            - Source the mount was gathered from, a file path for file based
+              sources or V(mount) for the output of the mount binary.
+          returned: always
+          type: str
+        note:
+          description:
+            - Additional information about the entry, set when the size
+              information could not be gathered due to a timeout and
+              O(on_timeout) is V(warn).
+          returned: when a timeout occurred and O(on_timeout) is V(warn)
+          type: str
+"""
+
+MOUNT_SOURCE = 'mount'
+STATIC_SOURCES = ('/etc/fstab',)
+DYNAMIC_SOURCES = ('/proc/mounts',)
+SOURCE_ALIASES = {
+    'all': STATIC_SOURCES + DYNAMIC_SOURCES + (MOUNT_SOURCE,),
+    'static': STATIC_SOURCES,
+    'dynamic': DYNAMIC_SOURCES,
+    MOUNT_SOURCE: (MOUNT_SOURCE,),
+}
+OCTAL_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(r'\\([0-7]{3})')
+UUID_RE = re.compile(r'^[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}(?:-[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}){3}-[0-9A-Fa-f]{12}$')
+TIMEOUT_RESULT = 'timeout'
+
+
+def _decode_octal_escapes(value):
+    """Decode the octal escape sequences (such as \\040) used in mount paths."""
+    return OCTAL_ESCAPE_RE.sub(lambda match: chr(int(match.group(1), 8)), value)
+
+
+def _new_entry(device, mount, fstype, options, dump=None, passno=None):
+    return {
+        'device': device,
+        'mount': mount,
+        'fstype': fstype,
+        'options': options,
+        'dump': dump,
+        'passno': passno,
+        'size_total': None,
+        'size_available': None,
+        'uuid': 'N/A',
+    }
+
+
+def parse_mount_lines(text):
+    """Parse fstab/mtab/proc mounts style lines.
+
+    Expected format: device mount-point fstype options [dump passno]
+    """
+    entries = []
+    for raw_line in text.splitlines():
+        line = raw_line.strip()
+        if not line or line.startswith('#'):
+            continue
+        fields = line.split()
+        if len(fields) < 4:
+            continue
+        entry = _new_entry(
+            _decode_octal_escapes(fields[0]),
+            _decode_octal_escapes(fields[1]),
+            fields[2],
+            fields[3],
+        )
+        if len(fields) >= 6:
+            try:
+                entry['dump'] = int(fields[4])
+            except ValueError:
+                pass
+            try:
+                entry['passno'] = int(fields[5])
+            except ValueError:
+                pass
+        entries.append(entry)
+    return entries
+
+
+def parse_mount_command_output(text):
+    """Parse the output of C(mount) or C(mount -l).
+
+    Expected format of modern implementations:
+        device on mount-point type fstype (options)
+    Older implementations report mtab style instead:
+        device mount-point fstype options [dump passno]
+    """
+    entries = []
+    for raw_line in text.splitlines():
+        line = raw_line.strip()
+        if not line:
+            continue
+        fields = line.split()
+        if len(fields) >= 5 and fields[1] == 'on' and fields[3] == 'type':
+            options = ' '.join(fields[5:]).strip()
+            if len(options) >= 2 and options.startswith('(') and options.endswith(')'):
+                options = options[1:-1].strip()
+            entry = _new_entry(
+                _decode_octal_escapes(fields[0]),
+                _decode_octal_escapes(fields[2]),
+                fields[4],
+                options,
+            )
+        elif len(fields) >= 4:
+            entry = _new_entry(
+                _decode_octal_escapes(fields[0]),
+                _decode_octal_escapes(fields[1]),
+                fields[2],
+                fields[3],
+            )
+            if len(fields) >= 6:
+                try:
+                    entry['dump'] = int(fields[4])
+                except ValueError:
+                    pass
+                try:
+                    entry['passno'] = int(fields[5])
+                except ValueError:
+                    pass
+        else:
+            continue
+        entries.append(entry)
+    return entries
+
+
+def expand_sources(sources):
+    """Expand source aliases to an ordered, de-duplicated list of sources."""
+    resolved = []
+    for source in sources:
+        resolved.extend(SOURCE_ALIASES.get(source, (source,)))
+    expanded = []
+    for source in resolved:
+        if source not in expanded:
+            expanded.append(source)
+    return expanded
+
+
+def entry_matches(entry, devices, fstypes):
+    """Return True when the entry matches the given fnmatch filters."""
+    if devices and not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(entry['device'], pattern) for pattern in devices):
+        return False
+    if fstypes and not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(entry['fstype'], pattern) for pattern in fstypes):
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def collect_uuid_maps(by_uuid_dir='/dev/disk/by-uuid'):
+    """Build UUID to device path and device path to UUID maps."""
+    uuid_to_device = {}
+    try:
+        uuid_names = os.listdir(by_uuid_dir)
+    except OSError:
+        return {}, {}
+    device_prefix = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(by_uuid_dir)) + os.sep
+    for uuid_name in uuid_names:
+        try:
+            target = os.readlink(os.path.join(by_uuid_dir, uuid_name))
+        except OSError:
+            continue
+        device = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(by_uuid_dir, target))
+        if device.startswith(device_prefix) and not device.endswith('/'):
+            uuid_to_device[uuid_name.lower()] = device
+    device_to_uuid = dict((device, uuid_name) for uuid_name, device in uuid_to_device.items())
+    return uuid_to_device, device_to_uuid
+
+
+def resolve_device_uuid(entry, uuid_to_device, device_to_uuid):
+    """Resolve UUID form devices to device paths and fill in the uuid fact."""
+    device = entry['device']
+    resolved_uuid = None
+    if device.upper().startswith('UUID='):
+        resolved_uuid = device[len('UUID='):]
+        device_path = uuid_to_device.get(resolved_uuid.lower())
+        if device_path:
+            entry['device'] = device_path
+    elif UUID_RE.match(device):
+        resolved_uuid = device
+        device_path = uuid_to_device.get(device.lower())
+        if device_path:
+            entry['device'] = device_path
+    entry['uuid'] = resolved_uuid or device_to_uuid.get(entry['device']) or 'N/A'
+
+
+def run_with_deadline(args, deadline):
+    """Run a command bounded by an absolute monotonic deadline.
+
+    Returns a (rc, stdout, stderr) tuple, C(TIMEOUT_RESULT) when the deadline
+    is exceeded and None when the command could not be started.
+    """
+    remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
+    if remaining <= 0:
+        return TIMEOUT_RESULT
+    try:
+        process = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
+    except (OSError, ValueError):
+        return None
+    try:
+        stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=remaining)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        process.kill()
+        try:
+            process.communicate(timeout=5)
+        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
+            pass
+        return TIMEOUT_RESULT
+    return (process.returncode, to_text(stdout, errors='replace'), to_text(stderr, errors='replace'))
+
+
+def get_mount_size(mount, deadline):
+    """Get (size_total, size_available) in bytes for a mount point.
+
+    Returns None when the size could not be determined and C(TIMEOUT_RESULT)
+    when the deadline was exceeded.
+    """
+    result = run_with_deadline(['df', '-P', '-k', mount], deadline)
+    if result is None or result == TIMEOUT_RESULT:
+        return result
+    rc, stdout, stderr = result
+    if rc != 0:
+        return None
+    lines = [line for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() if line.strip()]
+    if not lines:
+        return None
+    fields = lines[-1].split(None, 5)
+    if len(fields) < 5:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return int(fields[1]) * 1024, int(fields[3]) * 1024
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def gather_from_file(module, source, deadline):
+    """Gather mount entries from a fstab/mtab style file."""
+    try:
+        with open(source, 'rb') as source_file:
+            text = to_text(source_file.read(), errors='replace')
+    except (OSError, IOError) as exc:
+        module.warn('mount_facts: unable to read source %s: %s' % (source, exc))
+        return []
+    entries = parse_mount_lines(text)
+    for entry in entries:
+        entry['source'] = source
+    return entries
+
+
+def gather_from_mount_binary(module, mount_binary, deadline):
+    """Gather mount entries from the output of the mount binary."""
+    binary = mount_binary or module.get_bin_path('mount', required=False)
+    if not binary:
+        module.warn("mount_facts: unable to locate the 'mount' executable, skipping the 'mount' source")
+        return []
+    result = run_with_deadline([binary, '-l'], deadline)
+    if result is not None and result != TIMEOUT_RESULT and result[0] != 0:
+        # Some implementations of mount do not support -l, fall back to plain mount
+        result = run_with_deadline([binary], deadline)
+    if result == TIMEOUT_RESULT:
+        return []
+    if result is None:
+        module.warn("mount_facts: unable to run '%s' to gather mounts" % binary)
+        return []
+    rc, stdout, stderr = result
+    if rc != 0:
+        module.warn("mount_facts: '%s' failed (rc=%s): %s" % (binary, rc, stderr.strip()))
+        return []
+    entries = parse_mount_command_output(stdout)
+    for entry in entries:
+        entry['source'] = MOUNT_SOURCE
+    return entries
+
+
+def main():
+    module = AnsibleModule(
+        argument_spec=dict(
+            devices=dict(type='list', elements='str', required=False, default=None),
+            fstypes=dict(type='list', elements='str', required=False, default=None),
+            sources=dict(type='list', elements='str', required=False, default=['all']),
+            mount_binary=dict(type='str', required=False, default=None),
+            timeout=dict(type='float', required=False, default=10.0),
+            on_timeout=dict(type='str', choices=['error', 'warn', 'ignore'], required=False, default='warn'),
+            include_aggregate_mounts=dict(type='bool', required=False, default=False),
+        ),
+        supports_check_mode=True,
+    )
+
+    params = module.params
+    sources = expand_sources(params['sources'])
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + params['timeout']
+
+    entries = []
+    timed_out = False
+    for source in sources:
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            timed_out = True
+            break
+        if source == MOUNT_SOURCE:
+            entries.extend(gather_from_mount_binary(module, params['mount_binary'], deadline))
+        else:
+            entries.extend(gather_from_file(module, source, deadline))
+
+    devices = params['devices'] or []
+    fstypes = params['fstypes'] or []
+    filtered_entries = [entry for entry in entries if entry_matches(entry, devices, fstypes)]
+
+    uuid_to_device, device_to_uuid = collect_uuid_maps()
+    timeout_entries = None
+    for index, entry in enumerate(filtered_entries):
+        resolve_device_uuid(entry, uuid_to_device, device_to_uuid)
+        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
+        if remaining <= 0:
+            timed_out = True
+            timeout_entries = filtered_entries[index:]
+            break
+        size = get_mount_size(entry['mount'], deadline)
+        if size == TIMEOUT_RESULT:
+            timed_out = True
+            timeout_entries = filtered_entries[index:]
+            break
+        if size is not None:
+            entry['size_total'], entry['size_available'] = size
+
+    def build_facts():
+        mount_points = {}
+        for entry in filtered_entries:
+            mount_points.setdefault(entry['mount'], entry)
+        facts = {'mount_points': mount_points}
+        if params['include_aggregate_mounts']:
+            facts['aggregate_mounts'] = list(filtered_entries)
+        return facts
+
+    if timed_out:
+        pending_entries = timeout_entries if timeout_entries is not None else filtered_entries
+        mounts = ', '.join(entry['mount'] for entry in pending_entries)
+        if params['on_timeout'] == 'error':
+            module.fail_json(
+                msg='Timed out after %s seconds while gathering mount information for: %s'
+                    % (params['timeout'], mounts or 'no mounts'),
+                ansible_facts=build_facts(),
+            )
+        if params['on_timeout'] == 'warn':
+            module.warn('Timed out after %s seconds while gathering mount information for: %s'
+                        % (params['timeout'], mounts or 'no mounts'))
+            for entry in pending_entries:
+                entry['note'] = 'Could not get extra information due to timeout'
+        # 'ignore' silently continues without the extra information
+
+    facts = build_facts()
+
+    occurrence_count = {}
+    for entry in filtered_entries:
+        occurrence_count[entry['mount']] = occurrence_count.get(entry['mount'], 0) + 1
+    duplicates = sorted(mount for mount, count in occurrence_count.items() if count > 1)
+    if duplicates and not params['include_aggregate_mounts']:
+        module.warn('Duplicate mount points found (%s); mount_points only contains the first '
+                    'occurrence of each mount point. Set include_aggregate_mounts=true to also '
+                    'receive the complete list of all discovered mounts in aggregate_mounts.'
+                    % ', '.join(duplicates))
+
+    module.exit_json(changed=False, ansible_facts=facts)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+def main_runner(capfd):

+        if uuid_maps is None:

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+def test_parse_mount_lines():
+    entries = mount_facts.parse_mount_lines(FSTAB_TEXT)
+    assert len(entries) == 3
+    root = entries[0]

+    assert root['mount'] == '/'
+    assert root['fstype'] == 'ext4'
+    assert root['options'] == 'rw,noatime,nodiratime,data=ordered'
+    assert root['dump'] == 0

+    # A GPFS device that does not start with / must not be skipped

+def test_parse_mount_command_output():

+++ b/lib/ansible/module_utils/common/locale.py
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2020, Ansible Project
+# Simplified BSD License (see licenses/simplified_bsd.txt or https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-2-Clause)
+
+# Makes sure that Ansible modules can be written in any language.
+# The functions available here can be used to do many common tasks,
+# to simplify development of Python modules.
+
+from __future__ import absolute_import, division, print_function
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+from ansible.module_utils._text import to_native
+
+__all__ = ['get_best_parsable_locale']
+
+# Default order in which locales are preferred when choosing a locale
+# suitable for parsing command output that may contain Unicode text.
+DEFAULT_PREFERRED_LOCALES = ['C.utf8', 'en_US.utf8', 'C', 'POSIX']
+
+
+def get_best_parsable_locale(module, preferences=None):
+    """
+    Determine the best locale to use when parsing command output that
+    may involve Unicode parameters.
+
+    The available locales are enumerated by running ``locale -a`` on the
+    system and the first entry from the preference list (in order) that is
+    available is returned.  If none of the preferred locales are available
+    the 'C' locale is returned as a last resort.
+
+    :arg module: an AnsibleModule-compatible object exposing
+        ``get_bin_path`` and ``run_command``
+    :arg preferences: optional ordered list of locale names to try, most
+        preferred first.  When ``None`` the default preference order
+        (``DEFAULT_PREFERRED_LOCALES``) is used.
+    :rtype: str
+    :returns: the name of the selected locale
+    :raises RuntimeWarning: if the ``locale`` executable cannot be found,
+        if ``locale -a`` returns a non-zero return code, or if it produces
+        no output
+    """
+    if preferences is None:
+        preferences = DEFAULT_PREFERRED_LOCALES
+
+    try:
+        locale_bin = module.get_bin_path('locale')
+    except ValueError:
+        locale_bin = None
+
+    if locale_bin is None:
+        raise RuntimeWarning(
+            "Could not find the 'locale' executable on the system; cannot determine the best parsable locale")
+
+    rc, out, err = module.run_command([locale_bin, '-a'])
+
+    if rc != 0:
+        raise RuntimeWarning(
+            "Error running 'locale -a': return code %s, stderr: %s" % (rc, to_native(err)))
+
+    # blank lines are ignored
+    available_locales = [line for line in out.split('\n') if line]
+
+    if not available_locales:
+        raise RuntimeWarning(
+            "'locale -a' returned zero return code but no available locales were found in the output")
+
+    # exact string match against the available locales, in preference order
+    for preference in preferences:
+        if preference in available_locales:
+            return preference
+
+    # none of the preferred locales are available; 'C' is the last resort
+    return 'C'

+---
+minor_changes:
+  - Task executor now resolves the ``delegate_to`` value of a task once, before loop evaluation starts, avoiding double calculation of ``loop`` and ``delegate_to`` values (https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/78044).
+  - Add ``VariableManager.get_delegated_vars_and_hostname()`` which returns the final templated ``delegate_to`` hostname and the variables for the delegated-to host, centralizing delegation resolution in a single step.
+  - Add ``Task.get_play()`` which exposes the play a task belongs to by traversing its parent hierarchy.
+  - "``VariableManager.get_vars()`` no longer resolves ``delegate_to`` by default (``include_delegate_to`` now defaults to ``False``); the legacy delegation resolution path (``_get_delegated_vars``) is deprecated, and the internal ``_ansible_loop_cache`` workaround for loop evaluation caching has been removed."

+author: "Pluribus Networks (@rajaspachipulusu17)"

+short_description: CLI command to create/modify/delete user.
+description:
+  - This module can be used to create a user, modify a user's password and delete a user.
+options:
+  pn_cliswitch:
+    description:
+      - Target switch to run the CLI on.
+    required: false
+    type: str
+  state:
+    description:
+      - State the action to perform. Use C(present) to create user, C(update) to modify
+        user password and C(absent) to delete user.
+    required: true
+    type: str
+    choices: ['present', 'absent', 'update']
+  pn_name:
+    description:
+      - Name of the user.
+    required: true
+    type: str
+  pn_scope:
+    description:
+      - Scope of the user.
+    type: str
+    choices: ['local', 'fabric']
+  pn_password:
+    description:

+    type: str
+"""
+
+EXAMPLES = """
+- name: Create User functionality
+  pn_user:
+    pn_cliswitch: "sw01"
+    state: "present"
+    pn_name: "foo"
+    pn_scope: "local"
+    pn_password: "test123"
+
+- name: Modify User functionality
+  pn_user:
+    pn_cliswitch: "sw01"
+    state: "update"
+    pn_name: "foo"
+    pn_password: "test1234"
+
+- name: Delete User functionality
+  pn_user:
+    pn_cliswitch: "sw01"
+    state: "absent"
+    pn_name: "foo"
+"""
+
+RETURN = """
+command:
+  description: the CLI command run on the target node.
+  returned: always
+  type: str
+stdout:
+  description: set of responses from the user command.
+  returned: always
+  type: str
+stderr:
+  description: set of error responses from the user command.
+  returned: on error
+  type: str
+changed:
+  description: indicates whether the CLI caused changes on the target.
+  returned: always
+  type: bool
+"""
+
+
+from ansible.module_utils.basic import AnsibleModule
+from ansible.module_utils.network.netvisor.pn_nvos import pn_cli, run_cli
+
+
+def check_cli(module, cli):
+    """
+    This method checks for idempotency using the user-show command.
+    If a user with given name exists, return True else False.
+    :param module: The Ansible module to fetch input parameters
+    :param cli: The CLI string
+    """
+    name = module.params['pn_name']
+
+    cli += ' user-show name %s' % name
+    rc, out, err = module.run_command(cli, use_unsafe_shell=True)
+
+    out = out.split()
+    if name in out:
+        return True
+    else:
+        return False
+
+
+def main():
+    """ This section is for arguments parsing """
+
+    state_map = dict(
+        present='user-create',
+        absent='user-delete',
+        update='user-modify'
+    )
+
+    module = AnsibleModule(
+        argument_spec=dict(
+            pn_cliswitch=dict(required=False, type='str'),
+            state=dict(required=True, type='str',
+                       choices=state_map.keys()),
+            pn_name=dict(required=True, type='str'),
+            pn_scope=dict(required=False, type='str',
+                          choices=['local', 'fabric']),
+            pn_password=dict(required=False, type='str'),
+        ),
+        required_if=(
+            ["state", "present", ["pn_name", "pn_scope"]],
+            ["state", "update", ["pn_name", "pn_password"]],
+            ["state", "absent", ["pn_name"]],
+        )
+    )
+
+    # Accessing the arguments
+    cliswitch = module.params['pn_cliswitch']
+    state = module.params['state']
+    name = module.params['pn_name']
+    scope = module.params['pn_scope']
+    password = module.params['pn_password']
+
+    command = state_map[state]
+
+    # Building the CLI command string
+    cli = pn_cli(module, cliswitch)
+
+    NAME_EXISTS = check_cli(module, cli)
+
+    cli += ' %s name %s ' % (command, name)
+
+    if command == 'user-create':
+        if NAME_EXISTS is True:
+            module.exit_json(
+                skipped=True,
+                msg='user with name %s already exists' % name
+            )
+        if scope:
+            cli += ' scope ' + scope
+        if password:
+            cli += ' password ' + password
+    elif command == 'user-modify':
+        if NAME_EXISTS is False:
+            module.fail_json(
+                failed=True,
+                msg='user with name %s does not exist' % name
+            )
+        if password:
+            cli += ' password ' + password
+    elif command == 'user-delete':
+        if NAME_EXISTS is False:
+            module.exit_json(
+                skipped=True,
+                msg='user with name %s does not exist' % name
+            )
+
+    run_cli(module, cli, state_map)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+        end_match = re.match(r'^([a-zA-Z]+)\s+(.*)$', end)

+            name = start_match.group(1)
+            start_port = start_match.group(2).strip()
+        else:
+            name = prefix
+            start_port = start
+        if end_match:
+            end_port = end_match.group(2).strip()
+        else:
+            end_port = end
+        if name and name.startswith('ethe'):
+            name = 'ethernet'
+        start_parts = start_port.split('/')
+        end_parts = end_port.split('/')
+        try:
+            start_last = int(start_parts[-1])
+            end_last = int(end_parts[-1])
+        except ValueError:
+            return members
+        if end_last < start_last:
+            return members
+        base = start_parts[:-1]
+        for i in range(start_last, end_last + 1):
+            port = '/'.join(base + [str(i)])
+            members.append('%s %s' % (name, port) if name else port)
+    else:
+        for port in [p.strip() for p in ranges.split(',') if p.strip()]:
+            match = re.match(r'^([a-zA-Z]+)\s+(\d[\d/]*)$', port)
+            if match:
+                name = match.group(1)
+                if name.startswith('ethe'):
+                    name = 'ethernet'
+                members.append('%s %s' % (name, match.group(2)))
+            else:
+                members.append('%s %s' % (prefix, port) if prefix else port)
+    return members
+
+
+def is_member(member, lst):
+    """Check if a member is represented in a list of port definitions.
+
+    Each entry of I(lst) can be a single port or a port range; ranges
+    are expanded with range_to_members before the comparison. The
+    I(member) argument may also be a port range, in which case every
+    port of the range has to be present in the list.
+    """
+    expanded = list()
+    for item in lst:
+        if ' to ' in item:
+            expanded.extend(range_to_members(item, prefix='ethernet'))
+        else:
+            expanded.append(item)
+    if ' to ' in member:
+        member_ports = range_to_members(member, prefix='ethernet')
+        if not member_ports:
+            return False
+        return all(port in expanded for port in member_ports)
+    return member in expanded
+
+
+def search_obj_in_list(group, lst):
+    """Search for an object with a matching group id in a list of objects."""
+    for item in lst:
+        if item.get('group') == group:
+            return item
+    return None
+
+
+def map_config_to_obj(module):
+    """Parse the running configuration and return the LAG objects.
+
+    Returns a dict with the LAG group id as key and a dict holding the
+    group, name, mode, state and members of the LAG as value.
+    """
+    obj = {}
+    compare = module.params['check_running_config']
+    exec_command(module, 'skip')
+    out = get_config(module, compare=compare)
+
+    if not out:
+        return obj
+
+    current = None
+    for line in out.splitlines():
+        line = line.strip()
+        if not line or line.startswith('!'):
+            current = None
+            continue
+        lag_match = re.match(r'^lag\s+(.+?)\s+(dynamic|static)\s+id\s+(\d+)\s*$', line)
+        if lag_match:
+            name, mode, group = lag_match.group(1), lag_match.group(2), lag_match.group(3)
+            current = {
+                'group': str(group),
+                'name': name,
+                'mode': mode,
+                'state': 'present',
+                'members': list(),
+            }
+            obj[str(group)] = current
+            continue
+        if line.startswith('interface ') or line.startswith('hostname '):
+            current = None
+            continue
+        if current is not None:
+            if line.startswith('ports '):
+                current['members'].extend(range_to_members(line[6:].strip(), prefix='ethernet'))
+            elif line.startswith('disable'):
+                # LAG is administratively disabled, nothing to track
+                continue
+    return obj
+
+
+def map_params_to_obj(module):
+    """Build the list of desired LAG objects from the module parameters."""
+    obj = list()
+    keys = ['group', 'name', 'mode', 'members', 'state']
+
+    aggregate = module.params.get('aggregate')
+    if aggregate:
+        for item in aggregate:
+            config = {}
+            for key in keys:
+                if item.get(key) is not None:
+                    config[key] = item[key]
+                else:
+                    config[key] = module.params.get(key)
+            obj.append(config)
+    else:
+        config = {}
+        for key in keys:
+            config[key] = module.params.get(key)
+        obj.append(config)
+
+    for config in obj:
+        if config.get('group') is not None:
+            config['group'] = str(config['group'])
+
+    return obj
+
+
+def map_obj_to_commands(updates, module):
+    """Compute the commands required to move from have to want state."""
+    commands = list()
+    want, have = updates
+    purge = module.params['purge']
+
+    for w in want:
+        group = str(w['group'])
+        name = w.get('name')
+        mode = w.get('mode')
+        members = w.get('members') or []
+        state = w.get('state') or 'present'
+
+        h = search_obj_in_list(group, list(have.values()))
+
+        if state == 'absent':
+            if h:
+                name = name or h['name']
+                mode = mode or h['mode']
+                commands.append('no lag %s %s id %s' % (name, mode, h['group']))
+        elif not h:
+            if not name or not mode:
+                module.fail_json(msg='name and mode are required to create a link aggregation group')
+            commands.append('lag %s %s id %s' % (name, mode, group))
+            if members:
+                commands.append('ports %s' % ' '.join(members))
+            commands.append('exit')
+        else:
+            name = name or h['name']
+            mode = mode or h['mode']
+            have_members = h.get('members') or []
+            removed = [m for m in have_members if not is_member(m, members)]
+            added = [m for m in members if not is_member(m, have_members)]
+            if removed or added:
+                commands.append('lag %s %s id %s' % (name, mode, h['group']))
+                for m in removed:
+                    commands.append('no ports %s' % m)
+                if added:
+                    commands.append('ports %s' % ' '.join(added))
+                commands.append('exit')
+
+    if purge:
+        want_groups = [str(w['group']) for w in want]
+        for h in have.values():
+            if h['group'] not in want_groups:
+                commands.append('no lag %s %s id %s' % (h['name'], h['mode'], h['group']))
+
+    return commands
+
+
+def main():
+    """ entry point for module execution
+    """
+    element_spec = dict(
+        group=dict(type='str'),
+        name=dict(type='str'),
+        mode=dict(type='str', choices=['dynamic', 'static']),
+        members=dict(type='list', elements='str'),
+        state=dict(default='present', choices=['present', 'absent']),
+        check_running_config=dict(default=True, type='bool',
+                                  fallback=(env_fallback, ['ANSIBLE_CHECK_ICX_RUNNING_CONFIG']))
+    )
+
+    aggregate_spec = deepcopy(element_spec)
+    remove_default_spec(aggregate_spec)
+
+    argument_spec = dict(
+        aggregate=dict(type='list', elements='dict', options=aggregate_spec),
+        purge=dict(default=False, type='bool'),
+    )
+
+    argument_spec.update(element_spec)
+
+    required_one_of = [['aggregate', 'group']]
+    mutually_exclusive = [['aggregate', 'group']]
+
+    module = AnsibleModule(argument_spec=argument_spec,
+                           required_one_of=required_one_of,
+                           mutually_exclusive=mutually_exclusive,
+                           supports_check_mode=True)
+
+    results = {'changed': False}
+
+    want = map_params_to_obj(module)
+    have = map_config_to_obj(module)
+
+    commands = map_obj_to_commands((want, have), module)
+    results['commands'] = commands
+
+    if commands:
+        if not module.check_mode:
+            load_config(module, commands)
+
+        results['changed'] = True
+
+    module.exit_json(**results)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+def proxy_display(method):
+    """Decorator for ``Display`` methods (``display``, ``warning`` and
+    ``deprecated``) that proxies the call to the main process when running in
+    a forked worker process.

+    deprecation messages are handled (and deduplicated) once, in the main

+    default or synthesized kwargs are injected.

+            # and instead of displaying messages directly from the fork
+            # we will proxy them through the queue
+            return self._final_q.send_display(method.__name__, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        return method(self, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    return proxyit
+

+def _sanitize_key(key, no_log_strings, ignore_keys):
+    """
+    Helper function for :func:`sanitize_keys`.
+
+    :arg key: The mapping key to check for sensitive strings
+    :arg no_log_strings: list of native strings which must be redacted from key names
+    :arg ignore_keys: set of key names (matched by their full name) that must
+        be left untouched
+    :returns: the sanitized key.  Keys whose full name exactly matches an
+        entry of ``no_log_strings`` are replaced with
+        ``VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER``; keys containing a sensitive
+        string have that substring replaced with eight asterisks.  Non-string
+        keys, keys listed in ``ignore_keys`` and keys starting with
+        ``_ansible`` are returned unchanged.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(key, (text_type, binary_type)):
+        return key
+
+    native_key = to_native(key, errors='surrogate_or_strict')
+
+    if native_key in ignore_keys or native_key.startswith('_ansible'):
+        return key
+
+    if native_key in no_log_strings:
+        return 'VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER'
+
+    redacted_key = native_key
+    for omit_me in no_log_strings:
+        if omit_me in redacted_key:
+            redacted_key = redacted_key.replace(omit_me, '*' * 8)
+
+    # Return the original key object if nothing had to be redacted
+    if redacted_key == native_key:
+        return key
+
+    return redacted_key
+
+
+def _sanitize_keys_conditions(value, deferred_removals):
+    """
+    Helper function for :func:`sanitize_keys`.
+
+    :arg value: The value to check; if it is a container type (Mapping, Set or
+        Sequence) a new empty container of the same class is created and a
+        2-tuple of ``(value, new_container)`` is appended to
+        ``deferred_removals`` so the elements can be processed without deep
+        recursion; scalar values (including strings, which are Sequences) are
+        returned unchanged.
+    :returns: the new container, or the original value for scalars.
+    """
+    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
+        new_value = type(value)() if isinstance(value, MutableMapping) else {}
+    elif isinstance(value, Set):
+        new_value = type(value)() if isinstance(value, MutableSet) else set()
+    elif isinstance(value, Sequence) and not isinstance(value, (text_type, binary_type)):
+        # Need a mutable value to iterate into
+        new_value = type(value)() if isinstance(value, MutableSequence) else []
+    else:
+        return value
+    deferred_removals.append((value, new_value))
+    return new_value
+
+
+def sanitize_keys(obj, no_log_strings, ignore_keys=frozenset()):
+    """Sanitize keys in nested data structures
+
+    This function is a companion to :func:`remove_values`, which removes
+    sensitive values, while this function removes sensitive keys.  The two
+    functions are meant to be used together, with this function being called
+    first.
+
+    The function traverses the structure (using deferred removals instead of
+    deep recursion) and produces a new container in which any key name that
+    contains one of the strings in ``no_log_strings`` is redacted by
+    replacing the sensitive substring with eight asterisks (``********``),
+    while keys whose full name exactly matches an entry of
+    ``no_log_strings`` are replaced with the literal
+    ``VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER``.  Keys whose full name is listed
+    in ``ignore_keys`` or that start with ``_ansible`` are left untouched.
+
+    Objects that are not mappings (strings, numbers, booleans, ``None``,
+    sets, lists, tuples, :class:`~datetime.datetime` instances, ...) are
+    returned unchanged.  The class of each returned container is preserved.
+
+    :arg obj: The container object (Mapping, Sequence, Set, ...) whose keys
+        may need sanitizing; non-mapping objects are returned unchanged.
+    :arg no_log_strings: An iterable of strings (text or binary) whose
+        occurrences in key names must be redacted.  Each element is
+        converted to a native string via :func:`~ansible.module_utils.common.text.converters.to_native`.
+    :arg ignore_keys: A set of key names (matched by their full name) that
+        must not be sanitized.  Defaults to an empty set.
+    :returns: A copy of ``obj`` with the sensitive key names redacted, or
+        ``obj`` itself when it is not a mapping.
+    """
+    deferred_removals = deque()
+
+    if not isinstance(obj, Mapping):
+        return obj
+
+    no_log_strings = [to_native(s, errors='surrogate_or_strict') for s in no_log_strings]
+
+    new_obj = type(obj)() if isinstance(obj, MutableMapping) else {}
+    deferred_removals.append((obj, new_obj))
+
+    while deferred_removals:
+        old_data, new_data = deferred_removals.popleft()
+        if isinstance(new_data, Mapping):
+            for old_key, old_elem in old_data.items():
+                new_data[_sanitize_key(old_key, no_log_strings, ignore_keys)] = _sanitize_keys_conditions(old_elem, deferred_removals)
+        elif isinstance(new_data, MutableSequence):
+            for old_elem in old_data:
+                new_data.append(_sanitize_keys_conditions(old_elem, deferred_removals))
+        elif isinstance(new_data, MutableSet):
+            # Sets can only hold hashable elements, so no mapping (and thus
+            # no key) can be nested in them; copy the elements through as-is.
+            for old_elem in old_data:
+                new_data.add(old_elem)
+        else:
+            raise TypeError('Unknown container type encountered when sanitizing keys: %s' % type(new_data))
+
+    return new_obj
+

+        self.create_on_device()

+
+    def remove(self):
+        if self.module.check_mode:
+            return True
+        self.remove_from_device()
+        if self.exists():
+            raise F5ModuleError("Failed to remove the route")
+        return True
+
+    def should_update(self):
+        result = self._update_changed_options()
+        if result:

+        return False
+
+    def update(self):

+        diff = Difference(self.want, self.have)
+        updatables = Parameters.updatables
+        changed = dict()

+            change = diff.compare(k)
+            if change is None:
+                continue
+            else:
+                if isinstance(change, dict):

+            self.changes = UsableChanges(params=changed)

+        uri = "https://{0}:{1}/mgmt/tm/sys/message-routing/route/generic/{2}".format(
+            self.client.provider['server'],

+            self.client.provider['server'],
+            self.client.provider['server_port'],
+            transform_name(self.want.partition, self.want.name)

+            response = resp.json()
+        except ValueError as ex:
+            raise F5ModuleError(str(ex))
+
+        if 'code' in response and response['code'] == 400:
+            if 'message' in response:
+                raise F5ModuleError(response['message'])
+            else:

+class ModuleManager(object):
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):

+                "The current version of the device is not supported."

+        manager = self.get_manager('generic')

+    def version_less_than_14(self):
+        version = tmos_version(self.client)

+            state=dict(
+                default='present',
+                choices=['present', 'absent']
+            )
+        )

+        self.argument_spec.update(f5_argument_spec)

+def main():
+    spec = ArgumentSpec()
+
+    module = AnsibleModule(
+        argument_spec=spec.argument_spec,
+        supports_check_mode=spec.supports_check_mode
+    )
+
+    try:
+        mm = ModuleManager(module=module)
+        results = mm.exec_module()
+        module.exit_json(**results)
+    except F5ModuleError as ex:
+        module.fail_json(msg=str(ex))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+minor_changes:
+  - "ansible-galaxy collection build - the ``manifest`` key in ``galaxy.yml`` is now more flexible. When the key is absent it is internally represented by a distinct sentinel value (instead of an empty dict) so it is no longer confused with an explicitly provided falsy value. +    @staticmethod
+    def _valid_time_stamp(time_stamp_string):
+        """Validate and sanitize a ZIP file timestamp.
+
+        ZIP timestamps (as reported by ``zipinfo -T -s``) use the
+        YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS format, but some archives contain invalid values
+        (for example ``19800000.000000``), which used to make
+        ``time.strptime()`` raise a ValueError. This method extracts the
+        date components with a regular expression and validates them,
+        returning a ``time.struct_time`` compatible tuple. Any invalid or
+        out-of-range timestamp falls back to the ZIP epoch
+        (1980-01-01 00:00:00).
+
+        :param time_stamp_string: A timestamp string in YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS format.
+        :return: A 9-element tuple (year, month, day, hour, minute, second,
+            weekday, yearday, isdst) that can be passed to ``time.mktime()``.
+        """
+        # Default to the ZIP epoch for invalid or out-of-range timestamps
+        default_time_stamp = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
+
+        # Extract the date components from the YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS format
+        match = re.match(r'^(\d{4})(\d{2})(\d{2})\.(\d{2})(\d{2})(\d{2})$', time_stamp_string)
+        if not match:
+            return default_time_stamp
+
+        year = int(match.group(1))
+        month = int(match.group(2))
+        day = int(match.group(3))
+        hour = int(match.group(4))
+        minute = int(match.group(5))
+        second = int(match.group(6))
+
+        # ZIP file timestamps are only valid between 1980 and 2107
+        if not 1980 <= year <= 2107:
+            return default_time_stamp
+        if not 1 <= month <= 12:
+            return default_time_stamp
+        if not 1 <= day <= 31:
+            return default_time_stamp
+        if not 0 <= hour <= 23:
+            return default_time_stamp
+        if not 0 <= minute <= 59:
+            return default_time_stamp
+        if not 0 <= second <= 59:
+            return default_time_stamp
+
+        return (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, 0, 0, 0)

+def _find_clixml_header(data: bytes) -> int:
+    """
+    Scan ``data`` line by line and return the offset of the CLIXML header
+    marker (the ``#< CLIXML`` sequence, or just ``CLIXML`` when the marker
+    prefix is missing), or -1 when no CLIXML header is present.
+    """
+    offset = 0
+    length = len(data)
+    while offset < length:
+        eol = data.find(b"\r\n", offset)
+        if eol == -1:
+            line = data[offset:]
+            next_offset = length
+        else:
+            line = data[offset:eol]
+            next_offset = eol + 2
+
+        if b"CLIXML" in line:
+            marker = line.rfind(b"#< CLIXML")
+            if marker == -1:
+                marker = line.rfind(b"CLIXML")
+            return offset + marker
+
+        offset = next_offset
+
+    return -1
+
+
+def _replace_stderr_clixml(stderr: bytes) -> bytes:
+    """
+    Replace any CLIXML blocks embedded in ``stderr`` with their decoded content.
+
+    When PowerShell writes error output to stderr it can encode the content
+    as CLIXML. The CLIXML block is usually preceded and/or followed by other
+    (plain) output and may be spread over multiple lines, so the full stderr
+    stream cannot simply be passed to :func:`_parse_clixml`.
+
+    This scans ``stderr`` line by line for the CLIXML header and determines
+    the start and end of each CLIXML sequence (the header line up to the
+    closing ``</Objs>`` tag, including any ``<Objs>`` elements that directly
+    follow it as part of the same sequence). The block is decoded as UTF-8,
+    falling back to the Windows cp437 codepage before re-encoding to UTF-8
+    when the data is not valid UTF-8, parsed with :func:`_parse_clixml` and
+    replaced in place with the decoded text. All non-CLIXML lines, as well
+    as any data before or after a block (including trailing bytes on the
+    line of the closing tag), are preserved in their original order.
+    Incomplete or invalid CLIXML sequences, e.g. ones split over multiple
+    lines or missing their closing tag, are left unchanged.
+
+    :arg stderr: the raw stderr data as bytes
+    :returns: the stderr data as bytes, with any valid CLIXML blocks
+        replaced by their decoded content, or the input unchanged when no
+        valid CLIXML content is present
+    """
+    if b"CLIXML" not in stderr:
+        return stderr
+
+    result: list[bytes] = []
+    data = stderr
+    while True:
+        header_idx = _find_clixml_header(data)
+        if header_idx == -1:
+            result.append(data)
+            break
+
+        # The CLIXML sequence starts with the first <Objs element after the
+        # header and ends after the closing </Objs> tag
+        block_end = -1
+        pos = data.find(b"<Objs ", header_idx)
+        while pos != -1:
+            end_idx = data.find(b"</Objs>", pos)
+            if end_idx == -1:
+                # The sequence is incomplete (e.g. split over multiple lines
+                # or missing its closing tag), leave the data unchanged
+                return stderr
+
+            block_end = end_idx + len(b"</Objs>")
+
+            # Check if the sequence continues with another <Objs element
+            # directly after the current one (on the same line, or on the
+            # line right after it)
+            nxt = data.find(b"<Objs ", block_end)
+            if nxt == block_end:
+                pos = nxt
+            else:
+                line_end = data.find(b"\r\n", block_end)
+                if line_end != -1 and nxt == line_end + 2:
+                    pos = nxt
+                else:
+                    break
+
+        if block_end == -1:
+            # No <Objs element after the header, the CLIXML sequence is
+            # incomplete, leave the data unchanged
+            return stderr
+
+        # Decode the CLIXML block as UTF-8, falling back to the cp437
+        # codepage before re-encoding to UTF-8 when the data is not valid
+        # UTF-8
+        block = data[header_idx:block_end]
+        try:
+            block.decode("utf-8")
+        except UnicodeDecodeError:
+            block = block.decode("cp437").encode("utf-8")
+
+        try:
+            decoded = _parse_clixml(block)
+        except Exception:
+            # The block could not be parsed, leave the data unchanged
+            return stderr
+
+        # Replace the CLIXML block with the decoded text, preserving the
+        # data before the header and anything after </Objs> (including
+        # trailing bytes on the same line) in their original order
+        result.append(data[:header_idx])
+        result.append(decoded)
+        data = data[block_end:]
+
+    return b"".join(result)
+

+import { useState } from "react";
+
+import UIStore, { UI_EVENTS } from "../stores/UIStore";
+import { useEventEmitter } from "./useEventEmitter";
+
+/**
+ * Tracks the current window width, reported by the {@link UIStore}.
+ *
+ * The returned value is the current `UIStore.instance.windowWidth` and is
+ * updated whenever the store emits a {@link UI_EVENTS.Resize} event (for
+ * example when the window is resized).
+ *
+ * @returns The current window width in pixels.
+ */
+export function useWindowWidth(): number {
+    const [windowWidth, setWindowWidth] = useState<number>(UIStore.instance.windowWidth);
+
+    // Re-read the width from the store whenever a resize is emitted, so the
+    // hook stays in sync with UIStore.instance.windowWidth.
+    useEventEmitter(UIStore.instance, UI_EVENTS.Resize, () => {
+        setWindowWidth(UIStore.instance.windowWidth);
+    });
+
+    return windowWidth;
+}

+// Standard in-cluster deployment locations for Kubernetes service account
+// credentials. These are used as defaults when the corresponding configuration
+// values are not explicitly provided, enabling a Flipt deployment running inside
+// a Kubernetes cluster to authenticate with no explicit configuration.
+const (
+	// DefaultKubernetesServiceAccountTokenPath is the standard in-cluster path at
+	// which a pod's service account token is mounted.
+	DefaultKubernetesServiceAccountTokenPath = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"
+	// DefaultKubernetesCAPath is the standard in-cluster path at which the
+	// certificate authority used to validate the API server is mounted.
+	DefaultKubernetesCAPath = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt"
+
+	// KubernetesServiceHostEnvVar is the environment variable set by Kubernetes
+	// service discovery containing the API server host.
+	KubernetesServiceHostEnvVar = "KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST"
+	// KubernetesServicePortEnvVar is the environment variable set by Kubernetes
+	// service discovery containing the API server port.
+	KubernetesServicePortEnvVar = "KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT"
+)
+
+// AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig configures the Kubernetes authentication
+// method. This method authenticates requests using Kubernetes service account
+// tokens, validating them against the cluster's OIDC provider (the API server).
+//
+// When a field is left empty, a standard in-cluster deployment default is applied
+// (see Resolve), so an in-cluster Flipt deployment can enable the method with no
+// explicit configuration.
+type AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig struct {
+	// IssuerURL is the OIDC issuer URL of the Kubernetes API server.
+	// When empty, it is derived from the in-cluster service host and port
+	// (KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST / KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT) as https://<host>:<port>.
+	IssuerURL string `json:"issuerURL,omitempty" mapstructure:"issuer_url"`
+	// CAPath is the path to the certificate authority file used to validate the
+	// API server's TLS certificate. When empty, it defaults to the in-cluster CA
+	// mount (DefaultKubernetesCAPath).
+	CAPath string `json:"caPath,omitempty" mapstructure:"ca_path"`
+	// ServiceAccountTokenPath is the path to a service account token file.
+	// When empty, it defaults to the in-cluster service account token mount
+	// (DefaultKubernetesServiceAccountTokenPath).
+	ServiceAccountTokenPath string `json:"serviceAccountTokenPath,omitempty" mapstructure:"service_account_token_path"`
+}
+
+// ResolvedKubernetesConfig is the fully-resolved Kubernetes authentication
+// configuration with in-cluster defaults applied where values were omitted.
+type ResolvedKubernetesConfig struct {
+	// IssuerURL is the OIDC issuer of the Kubernetes API server.
+	IssuerURL string
+	// CAPath is the path to the CA certificate file used to validate the API server.
+	CAPath string
+	// ServiceAccountTokenPath is the path to a service account token file.
+	ServiceAccountTokenPath string
+}
+
+// Resolve applies in-cluster deployment defaults to the Kubernetes authentication
+// configuration and validates the result. It returns an error when the
+// configuration cannot be resolved (e.g. no issuer could be determined or the
+// issuer is not a well-formed URL).
+func (a AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig) Resolve() (ResolvedKubernetesConfig, error) {
+	var resolved ResolvedKubernetesConfig
+
+	// Resolve the issuer URL. An explicit value takes precedence; otherwise the
+	// in-cluster service host/port are used to derive the API server URL.
+	if a.IssuerURL != "" {
+		resolved.IssuerURL = a.IssuerURL
+	} else {
+		host := os.Getenv(KubernetesServiceHostEnvVar)
+		port := os.Getenv(KubernetesServicePortEnvVar)
+		if host == "" || port == "" {
+			return resolved, errFieldWrap("authentication.methods.kubernetes.issuer_url", errValidationRequired)
+		}
+		resolved.IssuerURL = fmt.Sprintf("https://%s:%s", host, port)
+	}
+
+	// The issuer must be a well-formed absolute http(s) URL.
+	u, err := url.Parse(resolved.IssuerURL)
+	if err != nil || u.Scheme == "" || u.Host == "" {
+		return resolved, errFieldWrap("authentication.methods.kubernetes.issuer_url", errInvalidURL)
+	}
+
+	// Resolve the CA path, defaulting to the in-cluster CA mount.
+	resolved.CAPath = a.CAPath
+	if resolved.CAPath == "" {
+		resolved.CAPath = DefaultKubernetesCAPath
+	}
+
+	// Resolve the service account token path, defaulting to the in-cluster mount.
+	resolved.ServiceAccountTokenPath = a.ServiceAccountTokenPath
+	if resolved.ServiceAccountTokenPath == "" {
+		resolved.ServiceAccountTokenPath = DefaultKubernetesServiceAccountTokenPath
+	}
+
+	return resolved, nil
+}
+
+// Info describes properties of the authentication method "kubernetes".
+func (a AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig) Info() AuthenticationMethodInfo {
+	info := AuthenticationMethodInfo{
+		Method:            auth.Method_METHOD_KUBERNETES,
+		SessionCompatible: false,
+	}
+
+	if a.IssuerURL != "" {
+		metadata := map[string]any{
+			"issuer_url": a.IssuerURL,
+		}
+		info.Metadata, _ = structpb.NewStruct(metadata)
+	}
+
+	return info
+}

+)
+
+// clearInClusterEnv ensures the in-cluster Kubernetes service discovery
+// environment variables are unset so tests are deterministic regardless of the
+// environment the tests run in.
+func clearInClusterEnv(t *testing.T) {

+	t.Setenv(KubernetesServicePortEnvVar, "")
+}
+
+func Test_AuthenticationMethods_AllMethods_IncludesKubernetes(t *testing.T) {

+
+	var found bool

+			found = true
+			assert.False(t, info.Enabled, "kubernetes should be disabled by default")
+			assert.False(t, info.SessionCompatible, "kubernetes is not a session method")
+		}

+	assert.True(t, found, "expected the kubernetes method to be exposed for introspection")

+
+func Test_AuthenticationKubernetes_SetDefaults(t *testing.T) {

+
+	v := viper.New()

+
+	// an enabled kubernetes method should be given a default cleanup schedule
+	assert.True(t, v.GetBool("authentication.methods.kubernetes.enabled"))
+	assert.Equal(t,
+		time.Duration(time.Hour), v.Get("authentication.methods.kubernetes.cleanup.interval"),
+		"expected a default cleanup interval for the enabled kubernetes method")

+		"expected a default cleanup grace period for the enabled kubernetes method")

+
+func Test_AuthenticationKubernetes_Validate_Valid(t *testing.T) {

+
+	c := &AuthenticationConfig{
+		Methods: AuthenticationMethods{
+			Kubernetes: AuthenticationMethod[AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig]{
+				Enabled: true,
+				Method: AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig{
+					IssuerURL: "https://kubernetes.default.svc",
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+	require.NoError(t, c.validate())
+}
+
+func Test_AuthenticationKubernetes_Validate_MissingIssuer(t *testing.T) {

+
+	c := &AuthenticationConfig{
+		Methods: AuthenticationMethods{
+			Kubernetes: AuthenticationMethod[AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig]{

+				Method:  AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig{
+					// no issuer and no in-cluster environment -> invalid
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+	err := c.validate()
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "kubernetes authentication")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "issuer_url")
+}
+
+func Test_AuthenticationKubernetes_Validate_InvalidIssuer(t *testing.T) {
+	clearInClusterEnv(t)
+
+	c := &AuthenticationConfig{
+		Methods: AuthenticationMethods{
+			Kubernetes: AuthenticationMethod[AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig]{
+				Enabled: true,
+				Method: AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig{
+					IssuerURL: "://not-a-valid-url",
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+	err := c.validate()
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "issuer_url")

+
+func Test_AuthenticationKubernetes_ShouldRunCleanup(t *testing.T) {
+	clearInClusterEnv(t)
+
+	// disabled method -> no cleanup
+	disabled := &AuthenticationConfig{
+		Methods: AuthenticationMethods{
+			Kubernetes: AuthenticationMethod[AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig]{
+				Enabled: false,
+				Method: AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig{
+					IssuerURL: "https://kubernetes.default.svc",
+				},
+				Cleanup: &AuthenticationCleanupSchedule{
+					Interval:    time.Hour,
+					GracePeriod: 30 * time.Minute,
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+	assert.False(t, disabled.ShouldRunCleanup())
+
+	// enabled method with a cleanup schedule -> cleanup runs
+	enabled := &AuthenticationConfig{
+		Methods: AuthenticationMethods{
+			Kubernetes: AuthenticationMethod[AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig]{
+				Enabled: true,
+				Method: AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig{
+					IssuerURL: "https://kubernetes.default.svc",
+				},
+				Cleanup: &AuthenticationCleanupSchedule{
+					Interval:    time.Hour,
+					GracePeriod: 30 * time.Minute,
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+	assert.True(t, enabled.ShouldRunCleanup())
+}
+
+func Test_AuthenticationKubernetes_Resolve_Defaults(t *testing.T) {

+	_, err := (AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig{}).Resolve()
+	require.Error(t, err)

+	t.Setenv(KubernetesServiceHostEnvVar, "kubernetes.default.svc")

+	assert.Equal(t, DefaultKubernetesServiceAccountTokenPath, resolved.ServiceAccountTokenPath)
+}

+package kubernetes
+
+import (
+	"context"
+
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/rpc/flipt/auth"
+)
+
+// GetAuthFunc is a function which retrieves an Authentication by the provided
+// client token. It matches the signature of the backing store's
+// GetAuthenticationByClientToken method.
+type GetAuthFunc func(ctx context.Context, clientToken string) (*auth.Authentication, error)
+
+// Authenticator wraps a primary client-token lookup (typically the backing
+// authentication store) with a fallback to Kubernetes service account token
+// validation.
+//
+// It satisfies the authentication Authenticator interface used by the
+// enforcement middleware. When a presented token is not known to the primary
+// lookup, it is validated as a Kubernetes service account token against the
+// cluster's OIDC provider, and the resulting Authentication is returned.
+// This allows static tokens (token method) and OIDC-issued tokens to continue
+// to be resolved from the store, while Kubernetes service account tokens are
+// validated on the fly.
+type Authenticator struct {
+	// Primary is the primary client-token lookup. When nil, only Kubernetes
+	// service account token validation is performed.
+	Primary GetAuthFunc
+	// Server is the Kubernetes authentication server used to validate
+	// service account tokens.
+	Server *Server
+}
+
+// GetAuthenticationByClientToken first consults the primary lookup. If the
+// token is unknown to the primary, it validates the token as a Kubernetes
+// service account token and returns the associated Authentication.
+func (a *Authenticator) GetAuthenticationByClientToken(ctx context.Context, clientToken string) (*auth.Authentication, error) {
+	if a.Primary != nil {
+		authentication, err := a.Primary(ctx, clientToken)
+		if err == nil {
+			return authentication, nil
+		}
+	}
+
+	return a.Server.Authenticate(ctx, clientToken)
+}

+package kubernetes_test
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	authserver "go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/server/auth"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/server/auth/method/kubernetes"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/storage/auth/memory"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/rpc/flipt/auth"
+	"go.uber.org/zap/zaptest"
+	"google.golang.org/grpc"
+	"google.golang.org/grpc/metadata"
+	"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/emptypb"
+)
+
+// Test_Authenticator_Middleware exercises the full enforcement path: a request
+// presenting a Kubernetes service account token as a Bearer credential is
+// authenticated by the gRPC unary interceptor via the kubernetes Authenticator.
+func Test_Authenticator_Middleware(t *testing.T) {
+	var (
+		ctx    = context.Background()
+		logger = zaptest.NewLogger(t)
+		store  = memory.NewStore()
+	)
+
+	tp, priv := startTestProvider(t)
+	caPath := testCAFile(t)
+	tokenPath := testTokenFile(t, "dummy-token")
+
+	kubeServer := kubernetes.NewServer(logger, store, kubernetesConfig(tp.Addr(), caPath, tokenPath))
+	require.NoError(t, kubeServer.Init(ctx))
+
+	authenticator := &kubernetes.Authenticator{
+		Primary: store.GetAuthenticationByClientToken,
+		Server:  kubeServer,
+	}
+
+	interceptor := authserver.UnaryInterceptor(logger, authenticator)
+
+	sub := "system:serviceaccount:default:middleware-sa"
+	exp := time.Now().UTC().Add(time.Hour)
+	saToken := signJWT(t, priv, saClaims(tp.Addr(), sub, map[string]any{
+		"kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/namespace":            "default",
+		"kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/service-account.name": "middleware-sa",
+	}, exp))
+
+	t.Run("service account token authenticates the request", func(t *testing.T) {
+		md := metadata.New(map[string]string{"authorization": "Bearer " + saToken})
+		callCtx := metadata.NewIncomingContext(context.Background(), md)
+
+		var saw *auth.Authentication
+		handler := func(ctx context.Context, _ interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
+			saw = authserver.GetAuthenticationFrom(ctx)
+			return &emptypb.Empty{}, nil
+		}
+
+		_, err := interceptor(callCtx, &emptypb.Empty{}, &grpc.UnaryServerInfo{FullMethod: "/flipt.auth/v1/Test/Call"}, handler)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.NotNil(t, saw, "expected the handler to observe an Authentication")
+		assert.Equal(t, auth.Method_METHOD_KUBERNETES, saw.Method)
+		assert.Equal(t, sub, saw.Metadata["io.flipt.auth.kubernetes.subject"])
+	})
+
+	t.Run("invalid token is rejected", func(t *testing.T) {
+		md := metadata.New(map[string]string{"authorization": "Bearer invalid-token"})
+		callCtx := metadata.NewIncomingContext(context.Background(), md)
+
+		handler := func(ctx context.Context, _ interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
+			t.Error("handler should not have been invoked")
+			return &emptypb.Empty{}, nil
+		}
+
+		_, err := interceptor(callCtx, &emptypb.Empty{}, &grpc.UnaryServerInfo{FullMethod: "/flipt.auth/v1/Test/Call"}, handler)
+		require.Error(t, err)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("no credentials are rejected", func(t *testing.T) {
+		callCtx := metadata.NewIncomingContext(context.Background(), metadata.New(nil))
+		handler := func(ctx context.Context, _ interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
+			t.Error("handler should not have been invoked")
+			return &emptypb.Empty{}, nil
+		}
+		_, err := interceptor(callCtx, &emptypb.Empty{}, &grpc.UnaryServerInfo{FullMethod: "/flipt.auth/v1/Test/Call"}, handler)
+		require.Error(t, err)
+	})
+}
