diff --git a/lib/auditd/auditd_linux.go b/lib/auditd/auditd_linux.go
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..8a98e62bd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/auditd/auditd_linux.go
@@ -0,0 +1,265 @@
+// Copyright 2023 Gravitational, Inc
+//
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+// you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+// You may obtain a copy of the License at
+//
+//      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+//
+// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+//go:build linux
+// +build linux
+
+package auditd
+
+import (
+	"encoding/binary"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+	"unsafe"
+
+	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink"
+	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink/nl"
+	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+)
+
+// nativeEndian is the byte order of the host platform. Netlink messages are
+// exchanged with the kernel in the host's native byte order.
+var nativeEndian = func() binary.ByteOrder {
+	var b [4]byte
+	*(*uint32)(unsafe.Pointer(&b[0])) = 1
+	if b[0] == 1 {
+		return binary.LittleEndian
+	}
+	return binary.BigEndian
+}()
+
+// NetlinkConnector abstracts a netlink connection used to communicate with
+// the kernel audit subsystem.
+type NetlinkConnector interface {
+	// Execute sends a netlink message to the kernel and returns the
+	// messages sent back in response to it.
+	Execute(msg netlink.Message) ([]netlink.Message, error)
+	// Receive reads pending netlink messages from the socket.
+	Receive() ([]netlink.Message, error)
+	// Close closes the netlink connection.
+	Close() error
+}
+
+// auditStatus is the status of the kernel audit subsystem as reported in
+// response to an AUDIT_GET request.
+type auditStatus struct {
+	// Enabled is true if the audit subsystem is enabled.
+	Enabled bool
+}
+
+// Client is a client for sending audit events to the kernel audit
+// subsystem (auditd).
+type Client struct {
+	// execName is the name of the executable sending the event.
+	execName string
+	// hostname is the hostname of the machine the event is sent from.
+	hostname string
+	// systemUser is the local *nix account the session runs as.
+	systemUser string
+	// teleportUser is the Teleport user performing the activity.
+	teleportUser string
+	// address is the address of the remote client.
+	address string
+	// ttyName is the name of the TTY allocated for the session.
+	ttyName string
+	// dial creates a new netlink connection. It can be replaced in tests.
+	dial func(family int, config *netlink.Config) (NetlinkConnector, error)
+	// conn is the established netlink connection, if any.
+	conn NetlinkConnector
+}
+
+// NewClient creates a new auditd Client from the given Message. The client
+// is not connected to the kernel audit subsystem until a message is sent.
+func NewClient(msg Message) *Client {
+	msg.SetDefaults()
+	return &Client{
+		execName:     msg.Exe,
+		hostname:     msg.Hostname,
+		systemUser:   msg.SystemUser,
+		teleportUser: msg.TeleportUser,
+		address:      msg.Address,
+		ttyName:      msg.TTYName,
+		dial:         dialNetlink,
+	}
+}
+
+// SendEvent sends a single audit event to the kernel audit subsystem. It
+// first checks whether the audit subsystem is enabled; if it is not, the
+// event is silently dropped and nil is returned.
+func SendEvent(event EventType, result ResultType, msg Message) error {
+	msg.SetDefaults()
+	client := NewClient(msg)
+	defer client.Close()
+	if err := client.SendMsg(event, result); err != nil {
+		if errors.Is(err, ErrAuditdDisabled) {
+			return nil
+		}
+		return err
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// IsLoginUIDSet returns true if the login UID for the current process is
+// set by the kernel. A login UID is required for the audit subsystem to
+// attribute events to a user login session.
+func IsLoginUIDSet() bool {
+	// The kernel reports the login UID of the current process in
+	// /proc/self/loginuid. An unset login UID is reported as 4294967295
+	// (KERNEL_AUDIT_UID).
+	data, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/self/loginuid")
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	uid := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
+	return uid != "" && uid != "4294967295"
+}
+
+// SendMsg sends a single audit event to the kernel audit subsystem. It
+// establishes a netlink connection if necessary, queries the status of the
+// audit subsystem, and only sends the event if the audit subsystem is
+// enabled.
+func (c *Client) SendMsg(event EventType, result ResultType) error {
+	if c.conn == nil {
+		conn, err := c.dial(nl.FAMILY_NETLINK, &netlink.Config{})
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get auditd status: %w", err)
+		}
+		c.conn = conn
+	}
+
+	status, err := c.getStatus(c.conn)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get auditd status: %w", err)
+	}
+	if !status.Enabled {
+		return ErrAuditdDisabled
+	}
+
+	payload := c.formatMessage(operationFor(event), result)
+	eventMsg := netlink.Message{
+		NlMsgHeader: netlink.NlMsgHeader{
+			Type:  uint16(event),
+			Flags: nl.NLM_F_REQUEST | nl.NLM_F_ACK,
+		},
+		Data: []byte(payload),
+	}
+	if _, err := c.conn.Execute(eventMsg); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to send audit event: %w", err)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// Close closes the netlink connection, if one was established.
+func (c *Client) Close() error {
+	if c.conn == nil {
+		return nil
+	}
+	err := c.conn.Close()
+	c.conn = nil
+	return err
+}
+
+// getStatus queries the kernel for the status of the audit subsystem using
+// an AUDIT_GET request.
+func (c *Client) getStatus(conn NetlinkConnector) (auditStatus, error) {
+	req := netlink.Message{
+		NlMsgHeader: netlink.NlMsgHeader{
+			Type:  uint16(AuditGet),
+			Flags: nl.NLM_F_REQUEST | nl.NLM_F_ACK,
+		},
+	}
+	resp, err := conn.Execute(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return auditStatus{}, err
+	}
+	for _, msg := range resp {
+		if msg.Type == uint16(AuditGet) {
+			return parseStatus(msg.Data)
+		}
+	}
+	return auditStatus{}, errors.New("no AUDIT_GET status response received")
+}
+
+// parseStatus decodes the payload of an AUDIT_GET response. The payload is
+// a struct audit_status; its first field is the enabled flag.
+func parseStatus(data []byte) (auditStatus, error) {
+	if len(data) < 4 {
+		return auditStatus{}, errors.New("invalid audit status payload")
+	}
+	// The audit status is decoded using the platform's native endianness,
+	// as the kernel sends it in the host byte order.
+	enabled := nativeEndian.Uint32(data[:4])
+	return auditStatus{Enabled: enabled == 1}, nil
+}
+
+// operationFor maps an audit event type to the value of the "op" field in
+// the audit message payload.
+func operationFor(event EventType) string {
+	switch event {
+	case AuditUserLogin:
+		return "login"
+	case AuditUserEnd:
+		return "session_close"
+	case AuditUserErr:
+		return "invalid_user"
+	default:
+		return UnknownValue
+	}
+}
+
+// formatMessage formats the audit message payload as space-separated
+// key=value pairs.
+func (c *Client) formatMessage(op string, result ResultType) string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "op=%s acct=%q exe=%q hostname=%s addr=%s terminal=%s",
+		op, c.systemUser, c.execName, c.hostname, c.address, c.ttyName)
+	if c.teleportUser != "" {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " teleportUser=%s", c.teleportUser)
+	}
+	fmt.Fprintf(&b, " res=%s", result)
+	return b.String()
+}
+
+// dialNetlink opens a netlink connection to the kernel audit subsystem.
+func dialNetlink(family int, config *netlink.Config) (NetlinkConnector, error) {
+	// Audit events are exchanged with the kernel over the NETLINK_AUDIT
+	// protocol.
+	if family != nl.FAMILY_NETLINK {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported netlink family: %v", family)
+	}
+	sock, err := nl.Dial(unix.NETLINK_AUDIT)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return &netlinkSocket{sock: sock}, nil
+}
+
+// netlinkSocket implements NetlinkConnector on top of an nl.Socket.
+type netlinkSocket struct {
+	sock *nl.Socket
+}
+

+// Package auditd provides an interface for reporting Teleport activity to
+// the Linux kernel audit subsystem (auditd).
+package auditd
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+)
+
+// EventType is the kernel code of an audit event, matching the values from
+// <linux/audit.h>.
+type EventType int
+
+// Audit event types.
+const (
+	// AuditGet is the code for the AUDIT_GET netlink message, which queries
+	// the status of the audit subsystem.
+	AuditGet EventType = 1000
+	// AuditUserEnd is the code for the AUDIT_USER_END netlink message, used
+	// to record the end of a user session.
+	AuditUserEnd EventType = 1005
+	// AuditUserLogin is the code for the AUDIT_USER_LOGIN netlink message,
+	// used to record a user login.
+	AuditUserLogin EventType = 1006
+	// AuditUserErr is the code for the AUDIT_USER_ERR netlink message, used
+	// to record an invalid user or authentication failure.
+	AuditUserErr EventType = 1007
+)
+
+// ResultType is the result of an audit event.
+type ResultType string
+
+// Audit event results.
+const (
+	// Success is the result for a successful event.
+	Success ResultType = "success"
+	// Failed is the result for a failed event.
+	Failed ResultType = "failed"
+)
+
+// UnknownValue is a placeholder used when a value is not available.
+const UnknownValue = "?"
+
+// ErrAuditdDisabled is returned when the kernel audit subsystem is not
+// enabled.
+var ErrAuditdDisabled = errors.New("auditd is disabled")
+
+// Message is the payload of an audit event. It contains the details of the
+// Teleport activity being recorded.
+type Message struct {
+	// Exe is the name of the executable sending the event (e.g.
+	// "teleport").
+	Exe string
+	// Hostname is the hostname of the machine the event was sent from.
+	Hostname string
+	// SystemUser is the local *nix account the session runs as.
+	SystemUser string
+	// TeleportUser is the Teleport user performing the activity.
+	TeleportUser string
+	// Address is the address of the remote client.
+	Address string
+	// TTYName is the name of the TTY allocated for the session (e.g.
+	// "pts/0").
+	TTYName string
+}
+
+// SetDefaults populates empty fields of the message with default values,
+// similar to how OpenSSH handles missing information in its audit logs.
+func (m *Message) SetDefaults() {
+	if m.Exe == "" {
+		m.Exe = "teleport"
+	}
+	if m.Hostname == "" {
+		m.Hostname = UnknownValue
+	}
+	if m.SystemUser == "" {
+		m.SystemUser = UnknownValue
+	}
+	if m.Address == "" {
+		m.Address = UnknownValue
+	}
+	if m.TTYName == "" {
+		m.TTYName = "teleport"
+	}
+}

+// Package netlink provides an interface for communicating with the Linux
+// kernel through netlink sockets.
+package netlink
+
+import (
+	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink/nl"
+)
+
+// Message is a netlink message, consisting of a standard header and an
+// optional payload.
+type Message = nl.Message
+
+// NlMsgHeader is the standard netlink message header.
+type NlMsgHeader = nl.NlMsgHeader
+
+// Socket is a bound netlink socket.
+type Socket = nl.Socket
+
+// NetlinkError is an error returned by the kernel in an NLMSG_ERROR message.
+type NetlinkError = nl.NetlinkError
+
+// Config is the configuration for a netlink connection.
+type Config struct {
+	// NetNS is the file descriptor of the target network namespace.
+	NetNS uint32
+}
+
+// Netlink message flags.
+const (
+	NLM_F_REQUEST  = nl.NLM_F_REQUEST
+	NLM_F_DUMP     = nl.NLM_F_DUMP
+	NLM_F_ACK      = nl.NLM_F_ACK
+	NLM_F_ACK_TLVS = nl.NLM_F_ACK_TLVS
+	NLM_F_EXCL     = nl.NLM_F_EXCL
+	NLM_F_CREATE   = nl.NLM_F_CREATE
+	NLM_F_REPLACE  = nl.NLM_F_REPLACE
+	NLM_F_APPEND   = nl.NLM_F_APPEND
+)
+
+// Netlink message types.
+const (
+	NLMSG_NOOP     = nl.NLMSG_NOOP
+	NLMSG_ERROR    = nl.NLMSG_ERROR
+	NLMSG_DONE     = nl.NLMSG_DONE
+	NLMSG_OVERRUN  = nl.NLMSG_OVERRUN
+	NLMSG_MIN_TYPE = nl.NLMSG_MIN_TYPE
+)
+
+// Address families.
+const (
+	FAMILY_ALL     = nl.FAMILY_ALL
+	FAMILY_V4      = nl.FAMILY_V4
+	FAMILY_V6      = nl.FAMILY_V6
+	FAMILY_NETLINK = nl.FAMILY_NETLINK
+)
+
+// Align aligns a netlink length.
+func Align(len int) int {
+	return nl.Align(len)
+}
+
+// ParseMessages parses a buffer containing one or more netlink messages.
+func ParseMessages(buf []byte) ([]Message, error) {
+	return nl.ParseMessages(buf)
+}
diff --git a/lib/netlink/nl/nl.go b/lib/netlink/nl/nl.go
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..2ef4ee61a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/netlink/nl/nl.go
@@ -0,0 +1,318 @@
+// Copyright 2023 Gravitational, Inc
+//
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+// you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+// You may obtain a copy of the License at
+//
+//      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+//
+// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+// WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+
+// Package nl provides low level access to Linux netlink sockets.
+package nl
+
+import (
+	"encoding/binary"
+	"errors"
+	"syscall"
+	"unsafe"
+
+	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+)
+
+const (
+	// NLMSG_ALIGNTO is the standard netlink buffer alignment.
+	NLMSG_ALIGNTO = 4
+	// NLMSG_HDRLEN is the standard netlink header length.
+	NLMSG_HDRLEN = 16
+)
+
+// Netlink message flags.
+const (
+	// NLM_F_REQUEST specifies that this message is a request.
+	NLM_F_REQUEST = 0x01
+	// NLM_F_DUMP requests a dump instead of a single response.
+	NLM_F_DUMP = 0x02
+	// NLM_F_ACK requests an NLMSG_ERROR ack for this message.
+	NLM_F_ACK = 0x04
+	// NLM_F_ACK_TLVS requests attribute values in the error response.
+	NLM_F_ACK_TLVS = 0x08
+	// NLM_F_EXCL is used with NLM_F_CREATE to request that the object
+	// must not already exist.
+	NLM_F_EXCL = 0x100
+	// NLM_F_CREATE creates the object if it does not exist.
+	NLM_F_CREATE = 0x400
+	// NLM_F_REPLACE replaces the object if it exists.
+	NLM_F_REPLACE = 0x800
+	// NLM_F_APPEND adds the object to the end of the list.
+	NLM_F_APPEND = 0x200
+)
+
+// Netlink message types.
+const (
+	// NLMSG_NOOP is a noop message.
+	NLMSG_NOOP = 0x01
+	// NLMSG_ERROR is an error response (or an ack when the error code is 0).
+	NLMSG_ERROR = 0x02
+	// NLMSG_DONE marks the end of a multi-part dump.
+	NLMSG_DONE = 0x03
+	// NLMSG_OVERRUN marks that data was lost in a multicast stream.
+	NLMSG_OVERRUN = 0x04
+	// NLMSG_MIN_TYPE is the minimum value for generic netlink message types.
+	NLMSG_MIN_TYPE = 0x10
+)
+
+// Address families.
+const (
+	// FAMILY_ALL matches all address families.
+	FAMILY_ALL = unix.AF_UNSPEC
+	// FAMILY_V4 is the IPv4 address family.
+	FAMILY_V4 = unix.AF_INET
+	// FAMILY_V6 is the IPv6 address family.
+	FAMILY_V6 = unix.AF_INET6
+	// FAMILY_NETLINK is the netlink address family.
+	FAMILY_NETLINK = unix.AF_NETLINK
+)
+
+// NlMsgHeader is the standard netlink message header. All multi-byte fields
+// are in the host's native byte order.
+type NlMsgHeader struct {
+	Len   uint32
+	Type  uint16
+	Flags uint16
+	Seq   uint32
+	Pid   uint32
+}
+
+// Message is a netlink message, consisting of a header and an optional
+// payload.
+type Message struct {
+	NlMsgHeader
+	Data []byte
+}
+
+// nativeEndian is the byte order of the host platform. Netlink messages are
+// exchanged with the kernel in the host's native byte order.
+var nativeEndian = func() binary.ByteOrder {
+	var b [4]byte
+	*(*uint32)(unsafe.Pointer(&b[0])) = 1
+	if b[0] == 1 {
+		return binary.LittleEndian
+	}
+	return binary.BigEndian
+}()
+
+// Align aligns a netlink length to NLMSG_ALIGNTO.
+func Align(len int) int {
+	return (len + NLMSG_ALIGNTO - 1) &^ (NLMSG_ALIGNTO - 1)
+}
+
+// Socket is a bound netlink socket.
+type Socket struct {
+	fd      int
+	seq     uint32
+	pending []byte
+}
+
+// Dial opens a raw netlink socket for the given protocol and binds it to the
+// kernel.
+func Dial(proto int) (*Socket, error) {
+	fd, err := unix.Socket(unix.AF_NETLINK, unix.SOCK_RAW, proto)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if err := unix.Bind(fd, &unix.SockaddrNetlink{Family: unix.AF_NETLINK}); err != nil {
+		unix.Close(fd)
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return &Socket{fd: fd}, nil
+}
+
+// Close closes the socket.
+func (s *Socket) Close() error {
+	return unix.Close(s.fd)
+}
+
+// Execute sends a message to the kernel and returns the messages sent back
+// in response to it, until an ack (NLMSG_ERROR) or the end of the reply
+// (NLMSG_DONE) is received.
+func (s *Socket) Execute(msg Message) ([]Message, error) {
+	if msg.Seq == 0 {
+		s.seq++
+		msg.Seq = s.seq
+	}
+	if err := s.send(msg); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	var pending []byte
+	var resp []Message
+	for {
+		// Consume all complete messages from the pending buffer.
+		consumed := false
+		for len(pending) >= NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+			m, rest, ok := parseOne(pending)
+			if !ok {
+				break
+			}
+			consumed = true
+			if m.Len < NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+				// Malformed message, skip it.
+				pending = rest
+				continue
+			}
+			switch m.Type {
+			case NLMSG_ERROR:
+				// An NLMSG_ERROR with an error code of 0 is an ack.
+				if len(m.Data) >= 4 {
+					if errno := int32(nativeEndian.Uint32(m.Data)); errno != 0 {
+						return nil, &NetlinkError{Errno: errno}
+					}
+				}
+				return resp, nil
+			case NLMSG_DONE:
+				return resp, nil
+			default:
+				resp = append(resp, m)
+			}
+			pending = rest
+		}
+		// Read more data from the socket.
+		buf := make([]byte, 8192)
+		n, _, err := unix.Recvfrom(s.fd, buf, 0)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		if n == 0 {
+			return nil, errors.New("netlink socket closed")
+		}
+		pending = append(pending, buf[:n]...)
+		_ = consumed
+	}
+}
+
+// Receive reads one batch of pending netlink messages from the socket. A
+// message that is only partially available is buffered and returned on a
+// subsequent call.
+func (s *Socket) Receive() ([]Message, error) {
+	var msgs []Message
+	for len(s.pending) >= NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+		m, rest, ok := parseOne(s.pending)
+		if !ok {
+			break
+		}
+		msgs = append(msgs, m)
+		s.pending = rest
+	}
+	if len(msgs) > 0 {
+		return msgs, nil
+	}
+	buf := make([]byte, 8192)
+	n, _, err := unix.Recvfrom(s.fd, buf, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if n == 0 {
+		return nil, errors.New("netlink socket closed")
+	}
+	s.pending = append(s.pending, buf[:n]...)
+	for len(s.pending) >= NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+		m, rest, ok := parseOne(s.pending)
+		if !ok {
+			break
+		}
+		msgs = append(msgs, m)
+		s.pending = rest
+	}
+	if len(msgs) == 0 {
+		// A partially received message will be completed by a later call.
+		if len(s.pending) == 0 {
+			return nil, errors.New("netlink socket closed")
+		}
+		return nil, nil
+	}
+	return msgs, nil
+}
+
+// send writes a single netlink message to the kernel.
+func (s *Socket) send(msg Message) error {
+	total := NLMSG_HDRLEN + Align(len(msg.Data))
+	buf := make([]byte, total)
+	msg.Len = uint32(total)
+	encodeHeader(buf, msg.NlMsgHeader)
+	copy(buf[NLMSG_HDRLEN:], msg.Data)
+	return unix.Sendto(s.fd, buf, 0, &unix.SockaddrNetlink{Family: unix.AF_NETLINK})
+}
+
+func encodeHeader(buf []byte, h NlMsgHeader) {
+	nativeEndian.PutUint32(buf[0:4], h.Len)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint16(buf[4:6], h.Type)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint16(buf[6:8], h.Flags)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint32(buf[8:12], h.Seq)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint32(buf[12:16], h.Pid)
+}
+
+// parseOne parses the first netlink message in buf, returning the message,
+// the remaining buffer, and whether a complete (or invalid) message was
+// found. If buf does not contain a complete message, ok is false.
+func parseOne(buf []byte) (Message, []byte, bool) {
+	if len(buf) < NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+		return Message{}, buf, false
+	}
+	var h NlMsgHeader
+	h.Len = nativeEndian.Uint32(buf[0:4])
+	h.Type = nativeEndian.Uint16(buf[4:6])
+	h.Flags = nativeEndian.Uint16(buf[6:8])
+	h.Seq = nativeEndian.Uint32(buf[8:12])
+	h.Pid = nativeEndian.Uint32(buf[12:16])
+
+	length := int(h.Len)
+	if length < NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+		// A malformed message; skip it so the caller is not stuck.
+		return Message{}, nil, true
+	}
+	if length > len(buf) {
+		// The message is only partially available.
+		return Message{}, buf, false
+	}
+	end := Align(length)
+	if end > len(buf) {
+		end = len(buf)
+	}
+	m := Message{NlMsgHeader: h, Data: buf[NLMSG_HDRLEN:length]}
+	return m, buf[end:], true
+}
+
+// ParseMessages parses a buffer containing one or more netlink messages.
+// An incomplete trailing message is ignored.
+func ParseMessages(buf []byte) ([]Message, error) {
+	var msgs []Message
+	for len(buf) >= NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+		m, rest, ok := parseOne(buf)
+		if !ok {
+			break
+		}
+		if m.Len >= NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+			msgs = append(msgs, m)
+		}
+		if len(rest) == 0 {
+			break
+		}
+		buf = rest
+	}
+	return msgs, nil
+}
+
+// NetlinkError is an error returned by the kernel in an NLMSG_ERROR message.
+type NetlinkError struct {
+	// Errno is the kernel error code.
+	Errno int32
+}
+
+// Error implements the error interface.
+func (e *NetlinkError) Error() string {
+	return "netlink error: " + syscall.Errno(int(e.Errno)).Error()
+}

+func ttyName(tty *os.File) (string, error) {
+	// /proc/self/fd/<fd> is a symlink to the device backing the file
+	// descriptor (e.g. /dev/pts/0).
+	linked, err := os.Readlink(fmt.Sprintf("/proc/self/fd/%v", tty.Fd()))

+func updateKubeConfig(cf *CLIConf, tc *client.TeleportClient) error {

+// returned values will switch the active kubeconfig context to it.
+//
+// If the tsh binary path is available and the Teleport cluster has Kubernetes
+// clusters registered, the returned values configure tsh as an exec auth
+// plugin. Otherwise, Values.Exec is left nil and static credentials are used.
+func buildKubeConfigUpdate(cf *CLIConf, tc *client.TeleportClient) (kubeconfig.Values, error) {

+	v.Credentials = key

+	// Fetch the list of known kubernetes clusters.
+	pc, err := tc.ConnectToProxy(cf.Context)
+	if err != nil {
+		return v, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	defer pc.Close()
+	ac, err := pc.ConnectToCurrentCluster(cf.Context, true)
+	if err != nil {

+	cn, err := ac.GetClusterName()
+	if err != nil {

+	kubeClusters, err := kubeutils.KubeClusterNames(cf.Context, ac)
+	if err != nil && !trace.IsNotFound(err) {
+		return v, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	// Only switch the kubeconfig context to the requested kubernetes

+// Package linux provides utilities for reading system metadata from Linux
+// system interfaces.
+package linux
+
+import (
+	"io/fs"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+)
+
+// DMIInfo holds information about the device acquired from the DMI (Desktop
+// Management Interface) sysfs interface.
+type DMIInfo struct {
+	// ProductName is the product name of the device, as read from the
+	// product_name file.
+	ProductName string
+	// ProductSerial is the product serial of the device, as read from the
+	// product_serial file.
+	ProductSerial string
+	// BoardSerial is the board serial of the device, as read from the
+	// board_serial file.
+	BoardSerial string
+	// ChassisAssetTag is the chassis asset tag of the device, as read from
+	// the chassis_asset_tag file.
+	ChassisAssetTag string
+}
+
+// DMIInfoFromSysfs reads the DMI information of the current system from
+// /sys/class/dmi/id.
+func DMIInfoFromSysfs() (*DMIInfo, error) {
+	return DMIInfoFromFS(os.DirFS("/sys/class/dmi/id"))
+}
+
+// DMIInfoFromFS reads the DMI information from the files in the provided
+// filesystem. It attempts to open and read the product_name, product_serial,
+// board_serial and chassis_asset_tag files, trimming any surrounding
+// whitespace from their contents.
+//
+// DMIInfoFromFS always returns a non-nil *DMIInfo populated with any data
+// that could be successfully read. Errors encountered while reading
+// individual files (for example permission denied) are aggregated and
+// returned along with the partially populated DMIInfo.
+func DMIInfoFromFS(dmifs fs.FS) (*DMIInfo, error) {
+	info := &DMIInfo{}
+
+	var errs []error
+	readFile := func(path string, field *string) {
+		data, err := fs.ReadFile(dmifs, path)
+		if err != nil {
+			errs = append(errs, trace.Wrap(err, "reading %q", path))
+			return
+		}
+		*field = strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
+	}
+
+	readFile("product_name", &info.ProductName)
+	readFile("product_serial", &info.ProductSerial)
+	readFile("board_serial", &info.BoardSerial)
+	readFile("chassis_asset_tag", &info.ChassisAssetTag)
+
+	return info, trace.NewAggregate(errs...)
+}

+
+package linux
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+)
+
+// OSRelease represents the parsed contents of an os-release file, as defined
+// by the os-release(5) specification:
+// https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/os-release.html
+type OSRelease struct {
+	// PrettyName is the value of the PRETTY_NAME field, e.g.
+	// "Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS".
+	PrettyName string
+	// Name is the value of the NAME field, e.g. "Ubuntu".
+	Name string
+	// VersionID is the value of the VERSION_ID field, e.g. "22.04".
+	VersionID string
+	// Version is the value of the VERSION field, e.g.
+	// "22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)".
+	Version string
+	// ID is the value of the ID field, e.g. "ubuntu".
+	ID string
+}
+
+// ParseOSRelease parses the contents of the /etc/os-release file.
+func ParseOSRelease() (*OSRelease, error) {
+	f, err := os.Open("/etc/os-release")
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	defer f.Close()
+
+	return ParseOSReleaseFromReader(f)
+}
+
+// ParseOSReleaseFromReader parses os-release key=value pairs from the
+// provided reader. Lines that are not of the form key=value are ignored, and
+// surrounding single and double quotes are trimmed from values before they
+// are stored.
+func ParseOSReleaseFromReader(in io.Reader) (*OSRelease, error) {
+	osr := &OSRelease{}
+
+	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(in)
+	for scanner.Scan() {
+		key, value, ok := strings.Cut(scanner.Text(), "=")
+		if !ok {
+			// Ignore lines that are not of the form key=value.
+			continue
+		}
+
+		value = strings.Trim(value, `"'`)
+		switch key {
+		case "PRETTY_NAME":
+			osr.PrettyName = value
+		case "NAME":
+			osr.Name = value
+		case "VERSION_ID":
+			osr.VersionID = value
+		case "VERSION":
+			osr.Version = value
+		case "ID":
+			osr.ID = value
+		}
+	}
+	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	return osr, nil
+}

+// Package keystore provides a common interface for storing and managing
+// cryptographic keys.
+package keystore
+
+import (
+	"bytes"

+	"crypto"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/types"
+

+
+// KeyStore abstracts the way Teleport stores keys.
+type KeyStore interface {
+	// GenerateKey generates a new RSA key, returns its identifier and
+	// a signer.
+	GenerateKey(ctx context.Context) (string, crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// GetSigner returns a signer for a previously generated key.
+	GetSigner(ctx context.Context, keyID string) (crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// SelectSSHKey returns a signer that can sign an SSH certificate for
+	// the provided CA.
+	SelectSSHKey(ctx context.Context, ca types.CertAuthority) (ssh.Signer, error)
+
+	// SelectTLSKey returns a certificate and a signer that can be used to
+	// create a TLS certificate for the provided CA.
+	SelectTLSKey(ctx context.Context, ca types.CertAuthority) ([]byte, crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// SelectJWTKey returns a signer that can sign JWTs for the provided CA.
+	SelectJWTKey(ctx context.Context, ca types.CertAuthority) (crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// DeleteKey deletes a key with the given identifier.
+	DeleteKey(ctx context.Context, keyID string) error
+}
+
+// pkcs11Prefix is the prefix of a PKCS#11 private key.
+const pkcs11Prefix = "pkcs11:"
+
+// KeyType returns the type of the provided private key. A key is
+// classified as PKCS11 if and only if it starts with the "pkcs11:"
+// prefix, otherwise it is classified as RAW.
+func KeyType(key []byte) types.PrivateKeyType {
+	if bytes.HasPrefix(key, []byte(pkcs11Prefix)) {
+		return types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11
+	}
+	return types.PrivateKeyType_RAW
+}

+		return nil, trace.NotFound("no SSH key pairs found in CA for %q", ca.GetClusterName())

+	keyPairs := ca.GetActiveKeys().TLS
+	if len(keyPairs) == 0 {
+		return nil, nil, trace.NotFound("no TLS key pairs found in CA for %q", ca.GetClusterName())

+			continue

+	}

+
+// parseSigner parses a private key in PKCS1, PKCS8 or OpenSSH PEM format and
+// returns a crypto.Signer.
+func parseSigner(key []byte) (crypto.Signer, error) {
+	parsed, err := ssh.ParseRawPrivateKey(key)
+	if err != nil {

+	}
+	switch k := parsed.(type) {
+	case *rsa.PrivateKey:
+		return k, nil
+	case *ecdsa.PrivateKey:

+	}

+
+// isRawKey returns true if the key described by the provided key type and
+// key material is a raw (PEM encoded) key and not a PKCS#11 one.
+func isRawKey(keyType types.PrivateKeyType, key []byte) bool {
+	if keyType == types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11 {

+	}
+	return KeyType(key) == types.PrivateKeyType_RAW
+}
+
+// newKeyID returns a new random opaque key identifier.
+func newKeyID() (string, error) {
+	buf := make([]byte, 16)
+	if _, err := rand.Read(buf); err != nil {
+		return "", trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	return hex.EncodeToString(buf), nil
+}

+++ b/openlibrary/solr/utils.py
@@ -0,0 +1,214 @@
+"""
+Solr utilities.
+
+Centralizes Solr configuration, shared state, and low-level Solr request
+handling so that the core update modules (e.g. ``openlibrary/solr/
+update_work.py``) can focus on building Solr documents without creating
+circular imports.
+"""
+
+import json
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+import httpx
+from httpx import HTTPError, HTTPStatusError, TimeoutException
+
+from openlibrary import config
+from openlibrary.solr.solr_types import SolrDocument
+from openlibrary.utils.retry import MaxRetriesExceeded, RetryStrategy
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("openlibrary.solr")
+
+solr_base_url: str | None = None
+solr_next: bool | None = None
+
+
+def load_config(c_config='conf/openlibrary.yml'):
+    """Load the Open Library config, if not already loaded."""
+    if not config.runtime_config:
+        config.load(c_config)
+        config.load_config(c_config)
+
+
+def get_solr_base_url() -> str:
+    """
+    Get Solr host
+
+    :rtype: str
+    """
+    global solr_base_url
+
+    load_config()
+
+    if not solr_base_url:
+        solr_base_url = config.runtime_config['plugin_worksearch']['solr_base_url']
+
+    return solr_base_url
+
+
+def set_solr_base_url(solr_url: str):
+    global solr_base_url
+    solr_base_url = solr_url
+
+
+def get_solr_next() -> bool:
+    """
+    Get whether this is the next version of solr; ie new schema configs/fields, etc.
+    """
+    global solr_next
+
+    if solr_next is None:
+        load_config()
+        solr_next = config.runtime_config['plugin_worksearch'].get('solr_next', False)
+
+    return solr_next
+
+
+def set_solr_next(val: bool):
+    global solr_next
+    solr_next = val
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SolrUpdateState:
+    """
+    A set of Solr update requests that can be made in one batch, including
+    the keys of the documents being updated, the documents to add/update,
+    the documents to delete, and whether to commit after the update.
+    """
+
+    keys: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Keys to update"""
+
+    adds: list[SolrDocument] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Records to be added/modified"""
+
+    deletes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Records to be deleted"""
+
+    commit: bool = False
+
+    # Override the + operator
+    def __add__(self, other):
+        if isinstance(other, SolrUpdateState):
+            return SolrUpdateState(
+                adds=self.adds + other.adds,
+                deletes=self.deletes + other.deletes,
+                keys=self.keys + other.keys,
+                commit=self.commit or other.commit,
+            )
+        else:
+            raise TypeError(f"Cannot add {type(self)} and {type(other)}")
+
+    def has_changes(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self.adds or self.deletes)
+
+    def to_solr_requests_json(self, indent: str | None = None, sep=',') -> str:
+        result = '{'
+        if self.deletes:
+            result += f'"delete": {json.dumps(self.deletes, indent=indent)}' + sep
+        for doc in self.adds:
+            result += f'"add": {json.dumps({"doc": doc}, indent=indent)}' + sep
+        if self.commit:
+            result += '"commit": {}' + sep
+
+        if result.endswith(sep):
+            result = result[: -len(sep)]
+        result += '}'
+        return result
+
+    def clear_requests(self) -> None:
+        self.adds.clear()
+        self.deletes.clear()
+
+
+async def solr_insert_documents(
+    documents: list[dict],
+    solr_base_url: str | None = None,
+    skip_id_check=False,
+):
+    """
+    Note: This has only been tested with Solr 8, but might work with Solr 3 as well.
+    """
+    solr_base_url = solr_base_url or get_solr_base_url()
+    params = {}
+    if skip_id_check:
+        params['overwrite'] = 'false'
+    logger.debug(f"POSTing update to {solr_base_url}/update {params}")
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
+        resp = await client.post(
+            f'{solr_base_url}/update',
+            timeout=30,  # seconds; the default timeout is silly short
+            params=params,
+            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
+            content=json.dumps(documents),
+        )
+    resp.raise_for_status()
+
+
+def solr_update(
+    update_request: SolrUpdateState,
+    skip_id_check=False,
+    solr_base_url: str | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    content = update_request.to_solr_requests_json()
+
+    solr_base_url = solr_base_url or get_solr_base_url()
+    params = {
+        # Don't fail the whole batch if one bad apple
+        'update.chain': 'tolerant-chain'
+    }
+    if skip_id_check:
+        params['overwrite'] = 'false'
+
+    def make_request():
+        logger.debug(f"POSTing update to {solr_base_url}/update {params}")
+        try:
+            resp = httpx.post(
+                f'{solr_base_url}/update',
+                # Large batches especially can take a decent chunk of time
+                timeout=300,
+                params=params,
+                headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
+                content=content,
+            )
+
+            if resp.status_code == 400:
+                resp_json = resp.json()
+
+                indiv_errors = resp_json.get('responseHeader', {}).get('errors', [])
+                if indiv_errors:
+                    for e in indiv_errors:
+                        logger.error(f'Individual Solr POST Error: {e}')
+
+                global_error = resp_json.get('error')
+                if global_error:
+                    logger.error(f'Global Solr POST Error: {global_error.get("msg")}')
+
+                if not (indiv_errors or global_error):
+                    # We can handle the above errors. Any other 400 status codes
+                    # are fatal and should cause a retry
+                    resp.raise_for_status()
+            else:
+                resp.raise_for_status()
+        except HTTPStatusError as e:
+            logger.error(f'HTTP Status Solr POST Error: {e}')
+            raise
+        except TimeoutException:
+            logger.error(f'Timeout Solr POST Error: {content}')
+            raise
+        except HTTPError as e:
+            logger.error(f'HTTP Solr POST Error: {e}')
+            raise
+
+    retry = RetryStrategy(
+        [HTTPStatusError, TimeoutException, HTTPError],
+        max_retries=5,
+        delay=8,
+    )
+
+    try:
+        return retry(make_request)
+    except MaxRetriesExceeded as e:
+        logger.error(f'Max retries exceeded for Solr POST: {e.last_exception}')

+def get_isbn_or_asin(isbn_or_asin: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """
+    Returns a tuple (isbn, asin) for the given identifier, with the unused
+    identifier set to an empty string. Amazon ASINs (identifiers starting
+    with "B", case-insensitive) are normalized to uppercase and returned in
+    the `asin` position; everything else is treated as an ISBN, normalized
+    via `canonical()`, and returned in the `isbn` position.
+
+    >>> get_isbn_or_asin("978-1-57607-945-4")
+    ('9781576079454', '')
+    >>> get_isbn_or_asin("b06xyhvxvj")
+    ('', 'B06XYHVXVJ')
+    >>> get_isbn_or_asin("")
+    ('', '')
+    """
+    if not isbn_or_asin:
+        return "", ""
+    if isbn_or_asin.strip().upper().startswith("B"):
+        return "", isbn_or_asin.strip().upper()
+    return canonical(isbn_or_asin), ""

+    True
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("", "B06XYHVXVJ")
+    True
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("123", "")
+    False
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("", "")
+    False
+    """

+    def get_work_reading_log(self, work_key: str) -> WorkReadingLogSolrSummary | None:
+        """
+        Returns the number of users who have the work in each preset reading
+        log shelf ("Want to Read", "Currently Reading", "Already Read"), in a
+        shape ready to be merged into the work's Solr document.
+
+        :param str work_key: type-prefixed work key (ex: /works/OL1W)
+        :rtype: WorkReadingLogSolrSummary | None
+        :return: the counts, or None if no reading-log data is available
+        """
+        work_id = int(work_key[len('/works/OL') : -len('W')])
+        # 1 = "Want to Read", 2 = "Currently Reading", 3 = "Already Read",
+        # see Bookshelves.PRESET_BOOKSHELVES.
+        result = self.db.query(
+            "SELECT"
+            " sum(CASE WHEN bookshelf_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)"
+            " AS want_to_read_count,"
+            " sum(CASE WHEN bookshelf_id = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)"
+            " AS currently_reading_count,"
+            " sum(CASE WHEN bookshelf_id = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)"
+            " AS already_read_count"
+            " FROM bookshelves_books"
+            " WHERE work_id=$work_id"
+            " AND bookshelf_id=ANY('{1,2,3}'::int[])",
+            vars={'work_id': work_id},
+        )
+        if not result:
+            return None
+        row = result[0]
+        want_to_read = row['want_to_read_count'] or 0
+        currently_reading = row['currently_reading_count'] or 0
+        already_read = row['already_read_count'] or 0
+        readinglog_count = want_to_read + currently_reading + already_read
+        if not readinglog_count:
+            return None
+        return {
+            'readinglog_count': readinglog_count,
+            'want_to_read_count': want_to_read,
+            'currently_reading_count': currently_reading,
+            'already_read_count': already_read,
+        }

+def get_language(language: str) -> str | None:
+    """
+    Return the MARC 21 language code corresponding to `language`, or None
+    if `language` is not recognized.
+
+    Accepts a wide range of ISO 639-1 and ISO 639-2 codes as well as
+    informal names, e.g. 'english', 'eng' and 'en' all map to 'eng', and
+    locale variants such as 'en_US' fall back to the base language code.
+    """
+    language = language.strip().casefold()
+    if code := LANGUAGES.get(language):
+        return code
+    # Locale variants, e.g. 'en_US' or 'pt-BR', fall back to the base
+    # language code, e.g. 'en' or 'pt'.
+    base = re.split(r'[-_]', language, maxsplit=1)[0]
+    if base != language:
+        return LANGUAGES.get(base)
+    return None

+    @staticmethod

diff --git a/scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py b/scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..eca51c2ef
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python
+"""Import Open Textbook Library (OTL) textbook metadata into Open Library.
+
+The Open Textbook Library is a curated collection of openly licensed
+textbooks hosted by the University of Minnesota:
+https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks
+
+This script streams the paginated JSON feed of textbooks from the OTL
+API, maps each record to an Open Library import record, and enqueues
+the records into a monthly batch import job.
+
+Run with a path to an openlibrary config file, eg:
+
+    python scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py conf/openlibrary.yml
+"""
+
+import json
+import time
+from collections.abc import Generator
+from typing import Any
+
+import requests
+
+from openlibrary.config import load_config
+from openlibrary.core.imports import Batch
+from scripts.solr_builder.solr_builder.fn_to_cli import FnToCLI
+
+FEED_URL = 'https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/api/textbooks'
+
+
+def get_feed() -> Generator[dict[str, Any], None, None]:
+    """Fetch and yield textbooks from the Open Textbook Library feed.
+
+    Starting from FEED_URL, each page of the API response is fetched,
+    every textbook dictionary found under the 'data' key is yielded,
+    and the 'links.next' URL is followed until no further page exists
+    in the API response.
+    """
+    url = FEED_URL
+    while url:
+        response = requests.get(url)
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        payload = response.json()
+        yield from payload.get('data', [])
+        url = payload.get('links', {}).get('next')
+
+
+def contributor_name(contributor: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    """Construct a contributor's name from their name components.
+
+    The name is built by concatenating the non-empty first_name,
+    middle_name and last_name values.
+    """
+    return ' '.join(
+        part
+        for part in (
+            contributor.get('first_name'),
+            contributor.get('middle_name'),
+            contributor.get('last_name'),
+        )
+        if part
+    )
+
+
+def is_primary_author(contributor: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    """Returns True if the contributor is marked as primary or an Author."""
+    return (
+        contributor.get('primary')
+        or contributor.get('is_primary')
+        or contributor.get('role') == 'Author'
+    )
+
+
+def subject_lc_classification(subject: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
+    """Returns the subject's LC call number, if available."""
+    return subject.get('lc_classification') or subject.get('lc_call_number') or subject.get('call_number')
+
+
+def map_data(data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Maps an Open Textbook Library record to an Open Library import record.
+
+    The raw OTL dictionary is transformed into an Open Library import
+    record with identifiers, core bibliographic fields, contributors,
+    subjects and classification metadata. Optional fields that are None
+    in the raw record are omitted from the import record.
+    """
+    record: dict[str, Any] = {
+        'title': data['title'],
+        'identifiers': {'open_textbook_library': str(data['id'])},
+        'source_records': [f'open_textbook_library:{data["id"]}'],
+    }
+
+    if data.get('isbn_10') is not None:
+        record['isbn_10'] = data['isbn_10']
+    if data.get('isbn_13') is not None:
+        record['isbn_13'] = data['isbn_13']
+    if data.get('language') is not None:
+        record['languages'] = [data['language']]
+    if data.get('description') is not None:
+        record['description'] = data['description']
+
+    authors: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+    contributions: list[str] = []
+    for contributor in data.get('contributors') or []:
+        name = contributor_name(contributor)
+        if is_primary_author(contributor):
+            authors.append({'name': name})
+        else:
+            contributions.append(name)
+    record['authors'] = authors
+    record['contributions'] = contributions
+
+    subjects = data.get('subjects') or []
+    record['subjects'] = [subject['name'] for subject in subjects]
+    lc_classifications = [
+        lc for lc in (subject_lc_classification(subject) for subject in subjects) if lc
+    ]
+    if lc_classifications:
+        record['lc_classifications'] = lc_classifications
+
+    publisher = data.get('publisher')
+    if publisher:
+        if isinstance(publisher, dict):
+            record['publishers'] = [publisher['name']]
+        else:
+            record['publishers'] = [p['name'] for p in publisher]
+
+    if data.get('copyright_year') is not None:
+        record['publish_date'] = str(data['copyright_year'])
+
+    return record
+
+
+def create_import_jobs(records: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
+    """Creates a batch import job for the given Open Library records.
+
+    Attempts to find the existing Open Textbook Library import batch
+    for the current year-month (named open_textbook_library-<YYYY><M>).
+    If nothing is found, a new batch is created. All of the given
+    import records are added to the batch job, each item keyed by its
+    source record identifier.
+    """
+    now = time.gmtime(time.time())
+    batch_name = f'open_textbook_library-{now.tm_year}{now.tm_mon}'
+    batch = Batch.find(batch_name) or Batch.new(batch_name)
+    batch.add_items([{'ia_id': record['source_records'][0], 'data': record} for record in records])
+
+
+def import_job(ol_config: str, dry_run: bool = False, limit: int = 10) -> None:
+    """Imports Open Textbook Library data into Open Library.
+
+    :param str ol_config: Path to openlibrary.yml file
+    :param bool dry_run: If true, only print out records to import
+    :param int limit: Maximum number of records to import
+    """
+    load_config(ol_config)
+
+    records = []
+    for entry in get_feed():
+        records.append(map_data(entry))
+        if len(records) >= limit:
+            break
+
+    if dry_run:
+        for record in records:
+            print(json.dumps(record))
+    else:
+        create_import_jobs(records)
+        print(f'{len(records)} entries added to the batch import job.')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    print('Start: Open Textbook Library import job')
+    FnToCLI(import_job).run()
+    print('End: Open Textbook Library import job')

+package mime
+
+import (
+	"sort"
+	"strings"
+
+	_ "embed"
+	goMime "mime"
+
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/conf"
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/log"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
+)
+
+//go:embed mime_types.yaml
+var mimeTypesFile string
+
+type mimeTypes struct {
+	Types    map[string]string `yaml:"types"`
+	Lossless []string          `yaml:"lossless"`
+}
+
+// LosslessFormats is the list of lossless audio formats (without the leading
+// dot), loaded from the mime_types.yaml configuration file.
+var LosslessFormats []string
+
+func init() {
+	conf.AddHook(LoadMimeTypes)
+}
+
+// LoadMimeTypes loads the MIME type definitions from the external
+// mime_types.yaml configuration file, registers them with the mime package
+// and populates LosslessFormats. It is run as a hook during application
+// startup, as soon as the configuration is loaded.
+func LoadMimeTypes() {
+	var config mimeTypes
+	if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(mimeTypesFile), &config); err != nil {
+		log.Error("Error parsing mime_types.yaml", err)
+		return
+	}
+	for extension, mimeType := range config.Types {
+		_ = goMime.AddExtensionType(extension, mimeType)
+	}
+	LosslessFormats = make([]string, 0, len(config.Lossless))
+	for _, extension := range config.Lossless {
+		LosslessFormats = append(LosslessFormats, strings.TrimPrefix(extension, "."))
+	}
+	sort.Strings(LosslessFormats)
+
+	// In some circumstances, Windows sets JS mime-type to `text/plain`!
+	_ = goMime.AddExtensionType(".js", "text/javascript")
+	_ = goMime.AddExtensionType(".css", "text/css")
+}

+// WithAdminUser adds an admin user to the context. If no admin user exists, it falls back to an
+// empty user. This is meant to be used in background tasks that need a user in the context.
+func WithAdminUser(ctx context.Context, ds model.DataStore) context.Context {
+	u, err := ds.User(ctx).FindFirstAdmin()
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Error(ctx, "No admin user found", err)
+		u = &model.User{}
+	}
+	ctx = request.WithUsername(ctx, u.UserName)
+	return request.WithUser(ctx, *u)
+}

+func tokenFromHeader(r *http.Request) string {

+	}

+	}

+// CRLFWriter returns an io.Writer that converts LF line endings to CRLF,
+// for use on Windows where editors and tools expect CRLF line endings.
+// Existing CRLF sequences are kept as they are, without any extra
+// conversion, and the conversion works correctly even when the data is
+// written in multiple steps (e.g. a "\r" and a "\n" written in separate
+// Write calls).
+func CRLFWriter(w io.Writer) io.Writer {
+	return &crlfWriter{w: w}
+}
+
+type crlfWriter struct {
+	w io.Writer
+	// lastWasCR is true when the last byte written to the underlying
+	// writer was a carriage return (\r)
+	lastWasCR bool
+}
+
+func (c *crlfWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	if len(p) == 0 {
+		return 0, nil
+	}
+	out := make([]byte, 0, len(p)+2)
+	for _, b := range p {
+		if b == '\n' && !c.lastWasCR {
+			out = append(out, '\r')
+		}
+		out = append(out, b)
+		c.lastWasCR = b == '\r'
+	}
+	n, err := c.w.Write(out)
+	if err != nil {
+		return n, err
+	}
+	return len(p), nil
+}

+package tmp_verify
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	_ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
+	"github.com/pocketbase/dbx"
+)
+
+type rowT struct {
+	ID   string     `db:"id"`
+	Name string     `db:"name"`
+	Exp  *time.Time `db:"expires_at"`
+	Upd  *time.Time `db:"updated_at"`
+}
+
+func TestNullScanIntoPointerTime(t *testing.T) {
+	db, err := dbx.Open("sqlite3", "file::memory:?cache=shared")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	defer db.Close()
+
+	if _, err = db.NewQuery(`create table t (id varchar primary key, name varchar, expires_at datetime, updated_at datetime)`).Execute(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	// Insert a row with NULL timestamps (the bug scenario)
+	if _, err = db.NewQuery(`insert into t (id, name) values ('1', 'x')`).Execute(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	// Insert a row with set timestamps
+	now := time.Now()
+	if _, err = db.NewQuery(`insert into t (id, name, expires_at, updated_at) values ('2', 'y', ?, ?)`).Bind(now.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), now.Format(time.RFC3339Nano)).Execute(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	var res []rowT
+	err = db.NewQuery(`select id, name, expires_at, updated_at from t order by id`).All(&res)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("scan failed: %v", err)
+	}
+	if len(res) != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("expected 2 rows, got %d", len(res))
+	}
+	// Row 1: NULL -> nil pointers, NO error
+	if res[0].Exp != nil || res[0].Upd != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("expected nil pointers for NULL row, got Exp=%v Upd=%v", res[0].Exp, res[0].Upd)
+	}
+	// Row 2: set -> non-nil pointers
+	if res[1].Exp == nil || res[1].Upd == nil {
+		t.Fatalf("expected non-nil pointers for set row, got Exp=%v Upd=%v", res[1].Exp, res[1].Upd)
+	}
+	t.Logf("OK: NULL row -> nil ptrs; set row -> non-nil ptrs (Exp=%v)", res[1].Exp)
+}

+# base language, based on Chromium's l10n fallback logic:
+#
+# - en: There is no en.pak file, so Chromium uses en-US.
+# - en-LR, en-PH: There is no .pak file for these, so Chromium uses en-US.
+# - pt: There is no pt.pak file, so Chromium uses pt-BR, the default
+#   Portuguese locale.
+# - pt-*: e.g. pt-PT, which might not have a .pak file, falls back to pt-BR.

+#   locale.
+# - zh-HK, zh-MO: These use traditional Chinese, so Chromium uses zh-TW.
+# - Other zh-*: Fall back to zh-CN.
+# - es-*: Fall back to the base language es.

+    'en': 'en-US',
+    'en-LR': 'en-US',
+    'en-PH': 'en-US',
+    'pt': 'pt-BR',
+    'zh': 'zh-CN',
+    'zh-HK': 'zh-TW',
+    'zh-MO': 'zh-TW',

+    ('zh-', 'zh-CN'),
+    ('es-', 'es'),

+    This is based on the LC_ALL / LC_MESSAGES / LANG environment variables,
+    as that's what QtWebEngine uses to determine the locale.

+    Return:

+        'en-US' rather than 'en_US.UTF-8'), or 'C' if no locale could be
+        determined.

+    loc = None
+    for var in ('LC_ALL', 'LC_MESSAGES', 'LANG'):

+    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
+        pass
+    else:
+        candidates.append(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(PyQt5.__file__),
+                                       'Qt5', 'resources', 'locales'))

+    # System installations, e.g. Arch Linux
+    candidates.append('/usr/share/qt5/qtwebengine_locales')
+    candidates.append('/usr/share/qtwebengine-locales')

+        language is the same as the locale).

+        if locale.startswith(prefix):

+def template_config_variables(template: str) -> typing.FrozenSet[str]:
+    """Find the config options referenced in a Jinja template.
+
+    Args:
+        template: A Jinja template.
+
+    Return:
+        A set of referenced config option names.
+
+    Raises:
+        NoOptionError: If a config option is not found.
+    """
+    # Importing the config module at module level would lead to a
+    # circular import.
+    from qutebrowser.config import config
+
+    env = jinja2.Environment()
+    ast = env.parse(template)
+
+    opts = set()
+    getattr_nodes = list(ast.find_all(jinja2.nodes.Getattr))
+    for node in getattr_nodes:
+        if not isinstance(node.attr, str):
+            continue
+
+        # We only care about the outermost attribute access of a chain,
+        # e.g. `min_chars` in `conf.hints.min_chars` - inner accesses
+        # are part of the same option name.
+        if any(n.node is node for n in getattr_nodes):
+            continue
+
+        # Walk down the chain of attribute accesses to find the root.
+        name_parts = [node.attr]
+        expr = node.node
+        while isinstance(expr, jinja2.nodes.Getattr) and \
+                isinstance(expr.attr, str):
+            name_parts.append(expr.attr)
+            expr = expr.node
+
+        # Only consider attribute accesses on the `conf` object, e.g.
+        # not `notconf.foo`.
+        if not (isinstance(expr, jinja2.nodes.Name) and
+                expr.name == 'conf'):
+            continue
+
+        name = '.'.join(reversed(name_parts))
+        config.instance.ensure_has_opt(name)
+        opts.add(name)
+
+    return frozenset(opts)
+
+

+"""A very simple parser for ELF files.
+
+This is *not* a full parser - it only implements enough of the ELF format
+to be able to find the `.rodata` section of the `libQt5WebEngineCore.so`
+library, in order to find the version of QtWebEngine and Chromium it was
+built with. The version strings are the only way to find that reliably,
+as the version in `PYQT_WEBENGINE_VERSION` is the version PyQt5 was
+compiled with, not necessarily the version of the Qt libraries in use.
+
+See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executable_and_Linkable_Format
+"""
+
+import os
+import re
+import mmap
+import enum
+import struct
+import dataclasses
+import typing
+
+if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from typing import IO
+
+
+class ParseError(Exception):
+    """Error parsing ELF files."""
+
+
+class Bitness(enum.Enum):
+    """Bitness of an ELF file."""
+
+    elf32 = 1
+    elf64 = 2
+
+
+class Endianness(enum.Enum):
+    """Endianness of an ELF file."""
+
+    little = 1
+    big = 2
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Ident:
+    """ELF identification.
+
+    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf#ELF_header
+    """
+
+    magic: bytes
+    class_: Bitness
+    data: Endianness
+    version: int
+    osabi: int
+    abiversion: int
+    pad: bytes
+
+    _SIZE = 16
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: 'IO[bytes]') -> 'Ident':
+        """Parse the ELF identification from a file.
+
+        https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf#ELF_header
+
+        Args:
+            fobj: A file object (or something similar, e.g. an mmap)
+                   to read from.
+
+        Raise:
+            ParseError: If the file doesn't look like an ELF file.
+        """
+        raw = fobj.read(cls._SIZE)
+        if len(raw) < cls._SIZE:
+            raise ParseError(
+                "File too short ({} bytes)".format(len(raw)))
+
+        magic = raw[:4]
+        if magic != b'\x7fELF':
+            raise ParseError("No ELF magic found")
+
+        try:
+            class_ = Bitness(raw[4])
+        except ValueError:
+            raise ParseError("Invalid ELF class {}".format(raw[4])) from None
+        try:
+            data = Endianness(raw[5])
+        except ValueError:
+            raise ParseError("Invalid ELF data encoding {}".format(raw[5]))\
+                from None
+
+        return cls(magic=magic,
+                   class_=class_,
+                   data=data,
+                   version=raw[6],
+                   osabi=raw[7],
+                   abiversion=raw[8],
+                   pad=raw[9:16])
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Header:
+    """ELF file header.
+
+    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf#The_file_header
+    """
+
+    e_type: int
+    e_machine: int
+    e_version: int
+    e_entry: int
+    e_phoff: int
+    e_shoff: int
+    e_flags: int
+    e_ehsize: int
+    e_phentsize: int
+    e_phnum: int
+    e_shentsize: int
+    e_shnum: int
+    e_shstrndx: int

+    # Format/size of the header after the identification, depending on
+    # the bitness. The byte order is native, as we only ever parse
+    # libraries of the current architecture.
+    _FORMATS = {
+        Bitness.elf32: ('=2H5I6H', 36),
+        Bitness.elf64: ('=2HIQQQI6H', 48),
+    }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: 'IO[bytes]', bitness: Bitness) -> 'Header':
+        """Parse the ELF file header from a file.
+
+        https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf#The_file_header
+
+        Args:
+            fobj: A file object (or something similar, e.g. an mmap)
+                   to read from.
+            bitness: The bitness of the ELF file (see the ELF
+                     identification).
+
+        Raise:
+            ParseError: If the file is too short.
+        """
+        fmt, size = cls._FORMATS[bitness]
+        raw = fobj.read(size)
+        if len(raw) < size:
+            raise ParseError(
+                "File too short ({} bytes)".format(len(raw)))
+        return cls(*struct.unpack(fmt, raw))

+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class SectionHeader:
+    """A section header of an ELF file.
+
+    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf#Section_header
+    """
+
+    sh_name: int
+    sh_type: int
+    sh_flags: int
+    sh_addr: int
+    sh_offset: int
+    sh_size: int
+    sh_link: int
+    sh_info: int
+    sh_addralign: int
+    sh_entsize: int

+    # byte order is native, as we only ever parse libraries of the
+    # current architecture.
+    _FORMATS = {
+        Bitness.elf32: ('=10I', 40),
+        Bitness.elf64: ('=2I4Q2I2Q', 64),
+    }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: 'IO[bytes]', bitness: Bitness) -> 'SectionHeader':
+        """Parse a section header from a file.
+
+        https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf#Section_header
+
+        Args:
+            fobj: A file object (or something similar, e.g. an mmap)
+                   to read from.
+            bitness: The bitness of the ELF file (see the ELF
+                     identification).
+
+        Raise:
+            ParseError: If the file is too short.
+        """
+        fmt, size = cls._FORMATS[bitness]
+        raw = fobj.read(size)
+        if len(raw) < size:
+            raise ParseError(
+                "File too short ({} bytes)".format(len(raw)))
+        return cls(*struct.unpack(fmt, raw))

+class Versions:
+    """QtWebEngine and Chromium versions found in an ELF file."""

+    chromium: str

+
+def _string_at(data: bytes, offset: int) -> str:
+    """Get a C string from `data` at the given `offset`.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the string is not terminated, the offset is out
+                    of bounds, or the string is not valid ASCII.
+    """
+    if offset >= len(data):
+        raise ParseError("String offset {} out of bounds".format(offset))
+    end = data.find(b'\x00', offset)
+    if end < 0:
+        raise ParseError("Unterminated string at offset {}".format(offset))
+    raw = data[offset:end]
+    try:
+        return raw.decode('ascii')
+    except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
+        raise ParseError("Invalid section name: {}".format(e)) from None
+
+
+def get_rodata_header(f: 'IO[bytes]') -> SectionHeader:
+    """Get the section header of the `.rodata` section of an ELF file.
+
+    Args:
+        f: A file object (or something similar, e.g. an mmap) pointing
+           to an ELF file.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the file is not a valid ELF file, or no `.rodata`
+                    section could be found.
+    """
+    ident = Ident.parse(f)
+    header = Header.parse(f, ident.class_)
+
+    if header.e_shnum == 0:
+        raise ParseError("No sections found")
+
+    f.seek(header.e_shoff)
+    sections = [SectionHeader.parse(f, ident.class_)
+                for _ in range(header.e_shnum)]
+
+    if header.e_shstrndx >= len(sections):
+        raise ParseError(
+            "Invalid section name string table index {}".format(
+                header.e_shstrndx))
+    strtab = sections[header.e_shstrndx]
+    f.seek(strtab.sh_offset)
+    names = f.read(strtab.sh_size)
+
+    for section in sections:
+        if _string_at(names, section.sh_name) == '.rodata':
+            return section
+
+    raise ParseError("No .rodata section found")
+
+
+def get_rodata(path: str) -> bytes:
+    """Read the contents of the `.rodata` section of an ELF file.
+
+    The file is memory mapped, as the libraries are large.
+
+    Args:
+        path: The path of the ELF file.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the file can't be read or parsed.
+    """
+    try:
+        f = open(path, 'rb')
+    except OSError as e:
+        raise ParseError("Failed to open {}: {}".format(path, e)) from None
+    with f:
+        try:
+            mm = mmap.mmap(f.fileno(), 0, prot=mmap.PROT_READ)
+        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
+            raise ParseError("Failed to mmap {}: {}".format(path, e)) from None
+        with mm:
+            try:
+                header = get_rodata_header(mm)
+                return bytes(mm[header.sh_offset:
+                                header.sh_offset + header.sh_size])
+            except ParseError as e:
+                raise ParseError("{}: {}".format(path, e)) from e
+
+
+_LIB_NAME = 'libQt5WebEngineCore.so.5'
+
+
+def _find_lib() -> str:
+    """Find the path of the QtWebEngineCore library.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the library could not be found.
+    """
+    import PyQt5
+    from PyQt5.QtCore import QLibraryInfo
+
+    pyqt_dir = os.path.dirname(PyQt5.__file__)
+    candidates = []
+    for libdir in (QLibraryInfo.location(QLibraryInfo.LibrariesPath),
+                   os.path.join(pyqt_dir, 'Qt5', 'lib'),
+                   os.path.join(pyqt_dir, 'Qt', 'lib')):
+        candidates.append(os.path.join(libdir, _LIB_NAME))
+
+    for path in candidates:
+        if os.path.exists(path):
+            return path
+
+    raise ParseError("QtWebEngineCore library not found")
+
+
+def parse_webenginecore() -> Versions:
+    """Parse the QtWebEngineCore library to find its versions.
+
+    The version of QtWebEngine and the Chromium version it contains are
+    stored as strings in the `.rodata` section of the library.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the library could not be found, the ELF file
+                    could not be parsed, or the version strings could
+                    not be found.
+    """
+    path = _find_lib()
+    try:
+        rodata = get_rodata(path)
+    except ParseError as e:
+        raise ParseError("Failed to read rodata of {}: {}".format(
+            path, e)) from e
+
+    # rodata also contains binary data, so we can't just decode it as
+    # utf-8 - latin-1 maps bytes 1:1 to unicode code points, so it
+    # never fails.
+    text = rodata.decode('latin-1')
+
+    webengine_match = re.search(r'QtWebEngine/([0-9.]+)', text)
+    if webengine_match is None:
+        raise ParseError("QtWebEngine version not found in rodata")
+
+    chromium_match = re.search(r'Chrome/([0-9.]+)', text)
+    if chromium_match is None:
+        raise ParseError("Chromium version not found in rodata")
+
+    return Versions(webengine=webengine_match.group(1),
+                    chromium=chromium_match.group(1))

+/**
+ * Generates a full social media URL from a {@link ContactSocialId} by combining the appropriate base url
+ * with the given username or url fragment.
+ *
+ * Known social media types (twitter, facebook, linked in, xing) are mapped to their standard base paths
+ * (e.g. {@code https://www.twitter.com/<user>}) as long as the given value does not already contain a
+ * scheme or {@code www.}. Inputs that already contain {@code http} or {@code www.} are returned as-is
+ * (after trimming surrounding whitespace). For other or custom sites only {@code https://} (and
+ * {@code www.} if missing) is prepended without appending a site specific path.
+ *
+ * This is the single normalization used by both the contact viewer (to render social links) and the

+export function getSocialUrl(contactId: ContactSocialId): string {
+	let socialUrlType = ""

+	const worldwidew = "www."
+	const socialId = contactId.socialId.trim()
+
+	if (socialId.indexOf("http") !== -1 || socialId.indexOf(worldwidew) !== -1) {
+		return socialId
+	}

+		case ContactSocialType.FACEBOOK:
+			socialUrlType = "facebook.com/"
+			break
+		case ContactSocialType.XING:

+			break
+		case ContactSocialType.LINKED_IN:
+			socialUrlType = "linkedin.com/in/"
+			break
+	}
+
+	return `${http}${worldwidew}${socialUrlType}${socialId}`
